option.name: F
option.para: Pass DTMF through the conference.

option.name: G

argument.name: x
argument.para: The file to playback

option.para: Play an intro announcement in conference.

option.name: i
option.para: Announce user join/leave with review.

option.name: I
option.para: Announce user join/leave without review.

option.name: k
option.para: Close the conference if there's only one active participant left at exit.

option.name: l
option.para: Set listen only mode (Listen only, no talking).

option.name: m
option.para: Set initially muted.

option.name: M
option.para: Enable music on hold when the conference has a single caller. Optionally, specify a musiconhold class to use. If one is not provided, it will use the channel's currently set music class, or default.

option.name: n
option.para: Disable the denoiser. By default, if func_speex is loaded, Asterisk will apply a denoiser to channels in the MeetMe conference. However, channel drivers that present audio with a varying rate will experience degraded performance with a denoiser attached. This parameter allows a channel joining the conference to choose not to have a denoiser attached without having to unload func_speex.

option.name: o
option.para: Set talker optimization - treats talkers who aren't speaking as being muted, meaning (a) No encode is done on transmission and (b) Received audio that is not registered as talking is omitted causing no buildup in background noise.

option.name: p
option.para: Allow user to exit the conference by pressing # (default) or any of the defined keys. Dial plan execution will continue at the next priority following MeetMe. The key used is set to channel variable MEETME_EXIT_KEY.

note.para: Option s has priority for * since it cannot change its activation code.

option.name: P
option.para: Always prompt for the pin even if it is specified.

option.name: q
option.para: Quiet mode (don't play enter/leave sounds).

option.name: r
option.para: Record conference (records as MEETME_RECORDINGFILE using format MEETME_RECORDINGFORMAT. Default filename is meetme-conf-rec-${CONFNO}-${UNIQUEID} and the default format is wav.

option.name: s
option.para: Present menu (user or admin) when * is received (send to menu).

option.name: t
option.para: Set talk only mode. (Talk only, no listening).

option.name: T
option.para: Set talker detection (sent to manager interface and meetme list).

option.name: v
option.para: Announce when a user is joining or leaving the conference. Use the voicemail greeting as the announcement. If the i or I options are set, the application will fall back to them if no voicemail greeting can be found.

argument.name: mailbox@[context]
argument.para: The mailbox and voicemail context to play from. If no context provided, assumed context is default.

option.name: w
option.para: Wait until the marked user enters the conference.

option.name: x
option.para: Leave the conference when the last marked user leaves.

option.name: X
option.para: Allow user to exit the conference by entering a valid single digit extension MEETME_EXIT_CONTEXT or the current context if that variable is not defined.

note.para: Option s has priority for * since it cannot change its activation code.

option.para: Do not play message when first person enters

option.name: S
option.para: Kick the user x seconds after he entered into the conference.

option.name: L
option.para: Limit the conference to x ms. Play a warning when y ms are left. Repeat the warning every z ms. The following special variables can be used with this option:

variable.name: CONF_LIMIT_TIMEOUT_FILE
variable.para: File to play when time is up.

variable.name: CONF_LIMIT_WARNING_FILE
variable.para: File to play as warning if y is defined. The default is to say the time remaining.

description.para: Enters the user into a specified MeetMe conference. If the confno is omitted, the user will be prompted to enter one. User can exit the conference by hangup, or if the p option is specified, by pressing #.

note.para: The DAHDI kernel modules and a functional DAHDI timing source (see dahdi_test) must be present for conferencing to operate properly. In addition, the chan_dahdi channel driver must be loaded for the i and r options to operate at all.

parameter.name: confno
parameter.para: Conference number.

description.para: Plays back the number of users in the specified MeetMe conference. If var is specified, playback will be skipped and the value will be returned in the variable. Upon application completion, MeetMeCount will hangup the channel, unless priority n+1 exists, in which case priority progress will continue.

option.name: M

option.name: n

option.name: N

option.name: r

option.name: R

option.name: s

option.name: S

option.name: t

option.name: T

option.name: u

application.name: ReceiveMF
application.synopsis: Detects MF digits on a channel and saves them to a variable.

parameter.name: variable
parameter.para: The input digits will be stored in the given variable name.

parameter.name: timeout
parameter.para: The number of seconds to wait for all digits, if greater than 0. Can be floating point. Default is no timeout.

option.name: d
option.para: Delay audio by a frame to try to extra quelch.

option.name: l
option.para: Receive digits even if a key pulse (KP) has not yet been received. By default, this application will ignore all other digits until a KP has been received.

option.name: k
option.para: Do not return a character for the KP digit.

option.name: m
option.para: Mute conference.

option.name: n
option.para: Maximum number of digits, regardless of the sequence.

option.name: o
option.para: Enable override. Repeated KPs will clear all previous digits.

option.name: q
option.para: Quelch MF from in-band.

option.name: r
option.para: "Radio" mode (relaxed MF).

option.name: s
option.para: Do not return a character for ST digits.

description.para: Reads a ST, STP, ST2P, or ST3P-terminated string of MF digits from the user in to the given variable.
This application does not automatically answer the channel and should be preceded with Answer or Progress as needed.

variable.name: RECEIVEMFSTATUS
variable.para: This is the status of the read operation.

application.name: SendMF
application.synopsis: Sends arbitrary MF digits on the current or specified channel.

parameter.name: digits
parameter.para: List of digits 0-9,*#ABC to send; w for a half-second pause, also f or F for a flash-hook if the channel supports flash-hook, h or H for 250 ms of 2600 Hz, and W for a wink if the channel supports wink.
Key pulse and start digits are not included automatically. * is used for KP, # for ST, A for STP, B for ST2P, and C for ST3P.

parameter.name: timeout_ms
parameter.para: Amount of time to wait in ms between tones. (defaults to 50ms).

parameter.name: duration_ms
parameter.para: Duration of each numeric digit (defaults to 55ms).

parameter.name: duration_ms_kp
parameter.para: Duration of KP digits (defaults to 120ms).

parameter.name: duration_ms_st
parameter.para: Duration of ST, STP, ST2P, and ST3P digits (defaults to 65ms).

parameter.name: channel
parameter.para: Channel where digits will be played

description.para: It will send all digits or terminate if it encounters an error.

manager.name: PlayMF
manager.synopsis: Play MF digit on a specific channel.

parameter.name: Channel
parameter.para: Channel name to send digit to.

parameter.name: Digit
parameter.para: The MF digit to play.

parameter.name: Duration
parameter.para: The duration, in milliseconds, of the digit to be played.

description.para: Plays an MF digit on the specified channel.

application.name: Milliwatt
application.synopsis: Generates a 1004 Hz test tone at 0dbm (mu-law).

option.name: m
option.para: Generate a 1004 Hz Milliwatt test tone at 0dbm, with a 1 second silent interval. This option must be specified if you are using this for a milliwatt test line.

option.name: o
option.para: Generate a constant tone at 1000 Hz like previous version.

description.para: Generates a 1004 Hz test tone.

By default, this application does not provide a Milliwatt test tone. It simply plays a 1004 Hz tone, which is not suitable for performing a milliwatt test. The m option should be used so that a real Milliwatt test tone is provided. This will include a 1 second silent interval every 10 seconds.
Previous versions of this application generated a constant tone at 1000 Hz. If for some reason you would prefer that behavior, supply the o option to get the old behavior.

function.name: MINIVMCOUNTER
function.synopsis: Reads or sets counters for MiniVoicemail message.

parameter.name: account
parameter.para: If account is given and it exists, the counter is specific for the account.
If account is a domain and the domain directory exists, counters are specific for a domain.

parameter.name: name
parameter.para: The name of the counter is a string, up to 10 characters.

parameter.name: operand
parameter.para: The counters never goes below zero. Valid operands for changing the value of a counter when assigning a value are:

enum.name: i
enum.para: Increment by value.

enum.name: d
enum.para: Decrement by value.

enum.name: s
enum.para: Set to value.

description.para: The operation is atomic and the counter is locked while changing the value. The counters are stored as text files in the minivm account directories. It might be better to use realtime functions if you are using a database to operate your Asterisk.

application.name: MixMonitor
application.synopsis: Record a call and mix the audio during the recording. Use of StopMixMonitor is required to guarantee the audio file is available for processing during dialplan execution.

argument.name: filename
argument.para: If filename is an absolute path, uses that path, otherwise creates the file in the configured monitoring directory from asterisk.conf.

option.name: a
option.para: Append to the file instead of overwriting it.

option.name: b
option.para: Only save audio to the file while the channel is bridged.

note.para: If you utilize this option inside a Local channel, you must make sure the Local channel is not optimized away. To do this, be sure to call your Local channel with the /n option. For example: Dial(Local/start@mycontext/n)

option.name: B
option.para: Play a periodic beep while this call is being recorded.

argument.name: interval
argument.para: Interval, in seconds. Default is 15.

option.name: c
option.para: Use the real Caller ID from the channel for the voicemail Caller ID.
By default, the Connected Line is used. If you want the channel caller's real number, you may need to specify this option.

option.name: d
option.para: Delete the recording file as soon as MixMonitor is done with it.
For example, if you use the m option to dispatch the recording to a voicemail box, you can specify this option to delete the original copy of it afterwards.

option.name: v
option.para: Adjust the heard volume by a factor of x (range -4 to 4)

option.name: V
option.para: Adjust the spoken volume by a factor of x (range -4 to 4)

option.name: W
option.para: Adjust both, heard and spoken volumes by a factor of x (range -4 to 4)

option.name: r
option.para: Use the specified file to record the receive audio feed. Like with the basic filename argument, if an absolute path isn't given, it will create the file in the configured monitoring directory.

option.name: t
option.para: Use the specified file to record the transmit audio feed. Like with the basic filename argument, if an absolute path isn't given, it will create the file in the configured monitoring directory.

option.name: D
option.para: Interleave the audio coming from the channel and the audio going to the channel and output it as a 2 channel (stereo) raw stream rather than mixing it. You must use the .raw file extension. Any other extension will produce a corrupted file.

option.name: n
option.para: When the r or t option is used, MixMonitor will insert silence into the specified files to maintain synchronization between them. Use this option to disable that behavior.

option.name: i
option.para: Stores the MixMonitor's ID on this channel variable.

option.name: p
option.para: Play a beep on the channel that starts the recording.

option.name: P
option.para: Play a beep on the channel that stops the recording.

option.name: m
option.para: Create a copy of the recording as a voicemail in the indicated mailbox(es) separated by commas eg. m(1111@default,2222@default,...). Folders can be optionally specified using the syntax: mailbox@context/folder

option.name: s
option.para: Don't record until seconds (can be fractional) have elapsed since MixMonitor was invoked. No audio is written to the recording file during this time. If the call ends before this period, no audio will be saved. This can be useful to avoid recording announcements, ringback tones, or other non-essential early audio.

parameter.name: command
parameter.para: Will be executed when the recording is over.
Any strings matching ^{X} will be unescaped to X.
All variables will be evaluated at the time MixMonitor is called.

warning.para: Do not use untrusted strings such as CALLERID(num) or CALLERID(name) as part of the command parameters. You risk a command injection attack executing arbitrary commands if the untrusted strings aren't filtered to remove dangerous characters. See function FILTER().

description.para: Records the audio on the current channel to the specified file.
This application does not automatically answer and should be preceded by an application such as Answer or Progress().

note.para: MixMonitor runs as an audiohook.

If a filename passed to MixMonitor ends with .wav49, Asterisk will silently convert the extension to .WAV for legacy reasons. MIXMONITOR_FILENAME will contain the actual filename that Asterisk is writing to, not necessarily the value that was passed in.

variable.name: MIXMONITOR_FILENAME
variable.para: Will contain the filename used to record.

warning.para: Do not use untrusted strings such as CALLERID(num) or CALLERID(name) as part of ANY of the application's parameters. You risk a command injection attack executing arbitrary commands if the untrusted strings aren't filtered to remove dangerous characters. See function FILTER().
When using the D option to save interleaved audio, you MUST use .raw as the file extension. Any other extension will produce a corrupted file.

application.name: StopMixMonitor
application.synopsis: Stop recording a call through MixMonitor, and free the recording's file handle.

parameter.name: MixMonitorID
parameter.para: If a valid ID is provided, then this command will stop only that specific MixMonitor.

description.para: Stops the audio recording that was started with a call to MixMonitor() on the current channel.

parameter.name: Channel
parameter.para: Used to specify the channel to mute.

parameter.name: Direction
parameter.para: Which part of the recording to mute: read, write or both (from channel, to channel or both channels).

parameter.name: State
parameter.para: Turn mute on or off : 1 to turn on, 0 to turn off.

description.para: This action may be used to mute a MixMonitor recording.

manager.name: MixMonitor
manager.synopsis: Record a call and mix the audio during the recording. Use of StopMixMonitor is required to guarantee the audio file is available for processing during dialplan execution.

parameter.name: Channel
parameter.para: Used to specify the channel to record.

parameter.name: File
parameter.para: Is the name of the file created in the monitor spool directory. Defaults to the same name as the channel (with slashes replaced with dashes). This argument is optional if you specify to record unidirectional audio with either the r(filename) or t(filename) options in the options field. If neither MIXMONITOR_FILENAME or this parameter is set, the mixed stream won't be recorded.

parameter.name: Options
parameter.para: Options that apply to the MixMonitor in the same way as they would apply if invoked from the MixMonitor application. For a list of available options, see the documentation for the mixmonitor application.

parameter.name: Command
parameter.para: Will be executed when the recording is over. Any strings matching ^{X} will be unescaped to X. All variables will be evaluated at the time MixMonitor is called.

warning.para: Do not use untrusted strings such as CALLERID(num) or CALLERID(name) as part of the command parameters. You risk a command injection attack executing arbitrary commands if the untrusted strings aren't filtered to remove dangerous characters. See function FILTER().

description.para: This action records the audio on the current channel to the specified file.

variable.name: MIXMONITOR_FILENAME
variable.para: Will contain the filename used to record the mixed stream.

manager.name: StopMixMonitor
manager.synopsis: Stop recording a call through MixMonitor, and free the recording's file handle.

parameter.name: Channel
parameter.para: The name of the channel monitored.

parameter.name: MixMonitorID
parameter.para: If a valid ID is provided, then this command will stop only that specific MixMonitor.

description.para: This action stops the audio recording that was started with the MixMonitor action on the current channel.

function.name: MIXMONITOR
function.synopsis: Retrieve data pertaining to specific instances of MixMonitor on a channel.

parameter.name: id
parameter.para: The unique ID of the MixMonitor instance. The unique ID can be retrieved through the channel variable used as an argument to the i option to MixMonitor.

parameter.name: key
parameter.para: The piece of data to retrieve from the MixMonitor.

managerEventInstance.synopsis: Raised when monitoring has started on a channel.
Raised when monitoring has stopped on a channel.
Raised when monitoring is muted or unmuted on a channel.

parameter.name: Direction
parameter.para: Which part of the recording was muted or unmuted: read, write or both (from channel, to channel or both directions).

parameter.name: State
parameter.para: If the monitoring was muted or unmuted: 1 when muted, 0 when unmuted.

parameter.name: string
parameter.para: String to playback as morse code to channel

description.para: Plays the Morse code equivalent of the passed string.
This application does not automatically answer and should be preceded by an application such as Answer() or Progress().
This application uses the following variables:

variable.name: MORSEDITLEN
variable.para: Use this value in (ms) for length of dit

variable.name: MORSETONE
variable.para: The pitch of the tone in (Hz), default is 800

variable.name: MORSESPACETONE
variable.para: The pitch of the spaces in (Hz), default is 0

variable.name: MORSETYPE
variable.para: The code type to use (AMERICAN for standard American Morse or INTERNATIONAL for international code. Default is INTERNATIONAL).

application.name: MP3Player
application.synopsis: Play an MP3 file or M3U playlist file or stream.

parameter.name: Location
parameter.para: Location of the file to be played. (argument passed to mpg123)

description.para: Executes mpg123 to play the given location, which typically would be a mp3 filename or m3u playlist filename or a URL. Please read https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M3U to see what the M3U playlist file format is like.
Note that mpg123 does not support HTTPS, so use HTTP for web streams.
User can exit by pressing any key on the dialpad, or by hanging up.
This application does not automatically answer and should be preceded by an application such as Answer() or Progress().

parameter.name: tech_data
parameter.para: Channel technology and data for creating the outbound channel. For example, SIP/1234.

parameter.name: type
parameter.para: This should be app or exten, depending on whether the outbound channel should be connected to an application or extension.

parameter.name: arg1
parameter.para: If the type is app, then this is the application name. If the type is exten, then this is the context that the channel will be sent to.

parameter.name: arg2
parameter.para: If the type is app, then this is the data passed as arguments to the application. If the type is exten, then this is the extension that the channel will be sent to.

parameter.name: arg3
parameter.para: If the type is exten, then this is the priority that the channel is sent to. If the type is app, then this parameter is ignored.

parameter.name: timeout
parameter.para: Timeout in seconds. Default is 30 seconds.

option.name: a
option.para: Originate asynchronously. In other words, continue in the dialplan without waiting for the originated channel to answer.

option.name: b
option.para: Before originating the outgoing call, Gosub to the specified location using the newly created channel.

option.name: B
option.para: Before originating the outgoing call, Gosub to the specified location using the current channel.

option.name: C
option.para: Comma-separated list of codecs to use for this call. Default is slin.

option.name: c
option.para: The caller ID number to use for the called channel. Default is the current channel's Caller ID number.

option.name: n
option.para: The caller ID name to use for the called channel. Default is the current channel's Caller ID name.

option.name: v
option.para: A series of channel variables to set on the destination channel.

description.para: This application originates an outbound call and connects it to a specified extension or application. This application will block until the outgoing call fails or gets answered, unless the async option is used. At that point, this application will exit with the status variable set and dialplan processing will continue.
This application sets the following channel variable before exiting:

variable.name: ORIGINATE_STATUS
variable.para: This indicates the result of the call origination.
variable.value: In practice, you should never see this value. Please report it to the issue tracker if you ever see it.

argument.name: Technology/Resource
argument.para: Specification of the device(s) to dial. These must be in the format of Technology/Resource, where Technology represents a particular channel driver, and Resource represents a resource available to that particular channel driver.

argument.name: Technology2/Resource2
argument.para: Optional extra devices to dial in parallel
If you need more than one, enter them as Technology2/Resource2& Technology3/Resource3&.....

option.name: b
option.para: Before initiating an outgoing call, Gosub to the specified location using the newly created channel. The Gosub will be executed for each destination channel.

option.name: B
option.para: Before initiating the outgoing call(s), Gosub to the specified location using the current channel.

option.name: d
option.para: Full duplex audio

option.name: i
option.para: Ignore attempts to forward the call

option.name: q
option.para: Quiet, do not play beep to caller

option.name: r
option.para: Record the page into a file (CONFBRIDGE(bridge,record_conference))

option.name: s
option.para: Only dial a channel if its device state says that it is NOT_INUSE

option.name: A

argument.name: x
argument.para: The announcement to playback to all devices

option.para: Play an announcement to all paged participants

option.name: n
option.para: Do not play announcement to caller (alters A(x) behavior)

parameter.name: timeout
parameter.para: Specify the length of time that the system will attempt to connect a call. After this duration, any page calls that have not been answered will be hung up by the system.

description.para: Places outbound calls to the given technology/resource and dumps them into a conference bridge as muted participants. The original caller is dumped into the conference as a speaker and the room is destroyed when the original caller leaves.

parameter.name: filenames
parameter.para: Ampersand separated list of filenames. If the filename is a relative filename (it does not begin with a slash), it will be searched for in the Asterisk sounds directory. If the filename is able to be parsed as a URL, Asterisk will download the file and then begin playback on it. To include a literal & in the URL you can enclose the URL in single quotes.

parameter.name: options
parameter.para: Comma separated list of options

option.name: skip
option.para: Do not play if not answered

option.name: noanswer
option.para: Playback without answering, otherwise the channel will be answered before the sound is played.

note.para: Not all channel types support playing messages while still on hook.

option.name: say
option.para: Play using the say.conf file.

option.name: mix
option.para: Play using a mix of filename and the say.conf file.

description.para: Plays back given filenames (do not put extension of wav/alaw etc). The Playback application answers the channel if no options are specified. If the file is non-existent it will fail.
This application sets the following channel variable upon completion:

variable.name: PLAYBACKSTATUS
variable.para: The status of the playback attempt as a text string.

description.para: See Also: Background (application) -- for playing sound files that are interruptible
WaitExten (application) -- wait for digits from caller, optionally play music on hold

parameter.name: arg
parameter.para: Arg is either the tone name defined in the indications.conf configuration file, or a directly specified list of frequencies and durations.

description.para: Plays a tone list. Execution will continue with the next step in the dialplan immediately while the tones continue to play.
See the sample indications.conf for a description of the specification of a tonelist.
Stop playing a tone list, initiated by PlayTones().

application.name: PrivacyManager
application.synopsis: Require phone number to be entered, if no CallerID sent

parameter.name: maxretries
parameter.para: Total tries caller is allowed to input a callerid. Defaults to 3.

parameter.name: minlength
parameter.para: Minimum allowable digits in the input callerid number. Defaults to 10.

parameter.name: options
parameter.para: Position reserved for options.

parameter.name: context
parameter.para: Context to check the given callerid against patterns.

description.para: If no Caller*ID is sent, PrivacyManager answers the channel and asks the caller to enter their phone number. The caller is given maxretries attempts to do so. The application does nothing if Caller*ID was received on the channel.
The application sets the following channel variable upon completion:

variable.name: PRIVACYMGRSTATUS
variable.para: The status of the privacy manager's attempt to collect a phone number from the user.

application.name: Queue
application.synopsis: Queue a call for a call queue.

option.name: b
option.para: Before initiating an outgoing call, Gosub to the specified location using the newly created channel. The Gosub will be executed for each destination channel.

option.name: B
option.para: Before initiating the outgoing call(s), Gosub to the specified location using the current channel.

option.name: C
option.para: Mark all calls as "answered elsewhere" when cancelled.

option.name: c
option.para: Continue in the dialplan if the callee hangs up.

option.name: d
option.para: Data-quality (modem) call (minimum delay).
This option only applies to DAHDI channels. By default, DTMF is verified by muting audio TX/RX to verify the tone is still present. This option disables that behavior.

option.name: F
option.para: When the caller hangs up, transfer the called member to the specified destination and start execution at that location.
NOTE: Any channel variables you want the called channel to inherit from the caller channel must be prefixed with one or two underbars ('_').
NOTE: Using this option from a Gosub() might not make sense as there would be no return points.

option.name: h
option.para: Allow callee to hang up by pressing *.

option.name: H
option.para: Allow caller to hang up by pressing *.

option.name: i
option.para: Ignore call forward requests from queue members and do nothing when they are requested.

option.name: I
option.para: Asterisk will ignore any connected line update requests or any redirecting party update requests it may receive on this dial attempt.

option.name: k
option.para: Allow the called party to enable parking of the call by sending the DTMF sequence defined for call parking in features.conf.

option.name: K
option.para: Allow the calling party to enable parking of the call by sending the DTMF sequence defined for call parking in features.conf.

option.name: m
option.para: Custom music on hold class to use, which will override the music on hold class configured in queues.conf, if specified.
Note that CHANNEL(musicclass), if set, will still override this option.

option.name: n
option.para: No retries on the timeout; will exit this application and go to the next step.

option.name: r
option.para: Ring instead of playing MOH. Periodic Announcements are still made, if applicable.

option.name: R
option.para: Ring instead of playing MOH when a member channel is actually ringing.

option.name: t
option.para: Allow the called user to transfer the calling user.

option.name: T
option.para: Allow the calling user to transfer the call.

option.name: x
option.para: Allow the called user to write the conversation to disk via MixMonitor.

option.name: X
option.para: Allow the calling user to write the conversation to disk via MixMonitor.

parameter.name: URL
parameter.para: URL will be sent to the called party if the channel supports it.

parameter.name: announceoverride
parameter.para: Announcement file(s) to play to agent before bridging call, overriding the announcement(s) configured in queues.conf, if any.

Ampersand separated list of filenames. If the filename is a relative filename (it does not begin with a slash), it will be searched for in the Asterisk sounds directory. If the filename is able to be parsed as a URL, Asterisk will download the file and then begin playback on it. To include a literal & in the URL you can enclose the URL in single quotes.

parameter.name: timeout
parameter.para: Will cause the queue to fail out after a specified number of seconds, checked between each queues.conf timeout and retry cycle.

parameter.name: AGI
parameter.para: Will setup an AGI script to be executed on the calling party's channel once they are connected to a queue member.

parameter.name: gosub
parameter.para: Will run a gosub on the called party's channel (the queue member) once the parties are connected. The subroutine execution starts in the named context at the s exten and priority 1.

note.para: Macro was removed in Asterisk 21 which resulted in an argument ordering change. The upgrade notice was missed for this, so a note is being made here to provide a record of the change for users who have not upgraded yet.

parameter.name: rule
parameter.para: Will cause the queue's defaultrule to be overridden by the rule specified.

parameter.name: position
parameter.para: Attempt to enter the caller into the queue at the numerical position specified. 1 would attempt to enter the caller at the head of the queue, and 3 would attempt to place the caller third in the queue.

description.para: In addition to transferring the call, a call may be parked and then picked up by another user.
This application will return to the dialplan if the queue does not exist, or any of the join options cause the caller to not enter the queue.
This application does not automatically answer and should be preceded by an application such as Answer(), Progress(), or Ringing().
This application sets the following channel variables upon completion:

variable.name: QUEUESTATUS
variable.para: The status of the call as a text string.

variable.name: ABANDONED
variable.para: If the call was not answered by an agent this variable will be TRUE.

variable.name: DIALEDPEERNUMBER
variable.para: Resource of the agent that was dialed set on the outbound channel.

variable.name: QUEUE_WITHDRAW_INFO
variable.para: If the call was successfully withdrawn from the queue, and the withdraw request was provided with optional withdraw info, the withdraw info will be stored in this variable.

variable.name: QUEUEWAIT
variable.para: The total amount of time, in seconds, that the caller spent waiting in the queue before being connected to an agent.

variable.name: QUEUEWAIT_MS
variable.para: The total amount of time, in milliseconds, that the caller spent waiting in the queue before being connected to an agent.

variable.name: ANSWEREDTIME
variable.para: The amount of time, in seconds, that the caller spent connected to an agent. If the call was never answered, this will be set to 0.

variable.name: ANSWEREDTIME_MS
variable.para: The amount of time, in milliseconds, that the caller spent connected to an agent.

variable.name: DIALEDTIME
variable.para: The total amount of time, in seconds, from the start of the call until it ends. This matches the behavior of Dial().

variable.name: DIALEDTIME_MS
variable.para: The total amount of time, in milliseconds, from the start of the call until it ends.

option.name: p
option.para: Add queue member in paused state.

option.name: r
option.para: Specify a reason why the member is in paused state.

description.para: Dynamically adds interface to an existing queue. If the interface is already in the queue it will return an error.
This application sets the following channel variable upon completion:

variable.name: AQMSTATUS
variable.para: The status of the attempt to add a queue member as a text string.

description.para: If the interface is NOT in the queue it will return an error.
This application sets the following channel variable upon completion:

parameter.name: reason
parameter.para: Is used to add extra information to the appropriate queue_log entries and manager events.

description.para: Pauses (blocks calls for) a queue member. The given interface will be paused in the given queue. This prevents any calls from being sent from the queue to the interface until it is unpaused with UnpauseQueueMember or the manager interface. If no queuename is given, the interface is paused in every queue it is a member of. The application will fail if the interface is not found.
This application sets the following channel variable upon completion:

variable.name: PQMSTATUS
variable.para: The status of the attempt to pause a queue member as a text string.

parameter.name: reason
parameter.para: Is used to add extra information to the appropriate queue_log entries and manager events.

description.para: Unpauses (resumes calls to) a queue member. This is the counterpart to PauseQueueMember() and operates exactly the same way, except it unpauses instead of pausing the given interface.
This application sets the following channel variable upon completion:

variable.name: UPQMSTATUS
variable.para: The status of the attempt to unpause a queue member as a text string.

description.para: Allows you to write your own events into the queue log.

application.name: QueueUpdate
application.synopsis: Writes to the queue_log file for outbound calls and updates Realtime Data. Is used at h extension to be able to have all the parameters.

description.para: Allows you to write Outbound events into the queue log.

example.title: Write outbound event into queue log

Returns 0 if queue is found and setqueuevar is defined, -1 otherwise.

function.name: QUEUE_MEMBER
function.synopsis: Provides a count of queue members based on the provided criteria, or updates a queue member's settings.

enum.name: logged
enum.para: Returns the number of logged-in members for the specified queue.

enum.name: free
enum.para: Returns the number of logged-in members for the specified queue that either can take calls or are currently wrapping up after a previous call.

enum.name: ready
enum.para: Returns the number of logged-in members for the specified queue that are immediately available to answer a call.

enum.name: count
enum.para: Returns the total number of members for the specified queue.

enum.name: penalty
enum.para: Gets or sets queue member penalty. If queuename is not specified when setting the penalty then the penalty is set in all queues the interface is a member.

enum.name: paused
enum.para: Gets or sets queue member paused status. If queuename is not specified when setting the paused status then the paused status is set in all queues the interface is a member.

enum.name: ringinuse
enum.para: Gets or sets queue member ringinuse. If queuename is not specified when setting ringinuse then ringinuse is set in all queues the interface is a member.

description.para: Allows access to queue counts [R] and member information [R/W].
queuename is required for all read operations.
interface is required for all member operations.

function.name: QUEUE_MEMBER_COUNT

warning.para: This function has been deprecated in favor of the QUEUE_MEMBER() function

function.name: QUEUE_GET_CHANNEL

parameter.name: variable
parameter.para: The input digits will be stored in the given variable name.

parameter.name: filenames
parameter.para: Ampersand separated list of filenames to play before reading digits or tone with option i. If the filename is a relative filename (it does not begin with a slash), it will be searched for in the Asterisk sounds directory. If the filename is able to be parsed as a URL, Asterisk will download the file and then begin playback on it. To include a literal & in the URL you can enclose the URL in single quotes.

parameter.name: maxdigits
parameter.para: Maximum acceptable number of digits. Stops reading after maxdigits have been entered (without requiring the user to press the # key).
Defaults to 0 - no limit - wait for the user press the # key. Any value below 0 means the same. Max accepted value is 255.

option.name: s
option.para: to return immediately if the line is not up.

option.name: i
option.para: to play filename as an indication tone from your indications.conf.

option.name: n
option.para: to read digits even if the line is not up.

application.name: SayCountedNoun
application.synopsis: Say a noun in declined form in order to count things

parameter.name: number
parameter.para: The number of things

parameter.name: filename
parameter.para: File name stem for the noun that is the name of the things

description.para: Selects and plays the proper singular or plural form of a noun when saying things such as "five calls". English has simple rules for deciding when to say "call" and when to say "calls", but other languages have complicated rules which would be extremely difficult to implement in the Asterisk dialplan language.

The correct sound file is selected by examining the number and adding the appropriate suffix to filename. If the channel language is English, then the suffix will be either empty or "s". If the channel language is Russian or some other Slavic language, then the suffix will be empty for nominative, "x1" for genative singular, and "x2" for genative plural.

Note that combining filename with a suffix will not necessarily produce a correctly spelled plural form. For example, SayCountedNoun(2,man) will play the sound file "mans" rather than "men". This behavior is intentional. Since the file name is never seen by the end user, there is no need to implement complicated spelling rules. We simply record the word "men" in the sound file named "mans".
This application does not automatically answer and should be preceded by an application such as Answer() or Progress.

application.synopsis: Say a adjective in declined form in order to count things

parameter.name: number
parameter.para: The number of things

parameter.name: filename
parameter.para: File name stem for the adjective

parameter.name: gender
parameter.para: The gender of the noun modified, one of 'm', 'f', 'n', or 'c'

description.para: Selects and plays the proper form of an adjective according to the gender and of the noun which it modifies and the number of objects named by the noun-verb combination which have been counted. Used when saying things such as "5 new messages". The various singular and plural forms of the adjective are selected by adding suffixes to filename.

If the channel language is English, then no suffix will ever be added (since, in English, adjectives are not declined). If the channel language is Russian or some other slavic language, then the suffix will the specified gender for nominative, and "x" for genative plural. (The genative singular is not used when counting things.) For example, SayCountedAdj(1,new,f) will play sound file "newa" (containing the word "novaya"), but SayCountedAdj(5,new,f) will play sound file "newx" (containing the word "novikh").
This application does not automatically answer and should be preceded by an application such as Answer(), Progress(), or Proceeding().

application.synopsis: Communicates with SMS service centres and SMS capable analogue phones.

parameter.para: The name of the queue used in /var/spool/asterisk/sms

description.para: SMS handles exchange of SMS data with a call to/from SMS capable phone or SMS PSTN service center. Can send and/or receive SMS messages. Works to ETSI ES 201 912; compatible with BT SMS PSTN service in UK and Telecom Italia in Italy. It has also been tested to work with DOMO phones from Telefónica Spain.
Typical usage is to use to handle calls from the SMS service centre CLI, or to set up a call using outgoing or manager interface to connect service centre to SMS().
"Messages are processed as per text file message queues. smsq (a separate software) is a command to generate message queues and send messages.

note.para: The protocol has tight delay bounds. Please use short frames and disable/keep short the jitter buffer on the ATA to make sure that responses (ACK etc.) are received in time.
It is also important to adjust the gain dB of the ATA. Some Telefónica DOMO Mensajes phones may require the gain to be set to +3dB, and others even up to +6dB, in order to work.

Default: all connected applications

parameter.name: args
parameter.para: Optional colon-delimited arguments passed to the winning application via the StasisStart event. These are equivalent to the extra arguments in Stasis().
Example: sales:priority-high

parameter.name: notify_claimed
parameter.para: Whether to send a CallClaimed event to ARI applications when a channel is claimed.
When enabled, the CallClaimed event is sent only to applications that matched the app_filter (or all applications if no filter was set).
Disabled by default to minimise WebSocket traffic under high load. Losing claimants already receive a 409 HTTP response.
Default: no

description.para: Broadcasts the incoming channel to all connected ARI applications (or a filtered subset) via a CallBroadcast event. ARI applications can respond with a claim request. The first application to claim the channel wins, and subsequent claims are rejected.

If an application claims the channel within the timeout, the channel is automatically placed under Stasis control with the winning application, exactly as if Stasis(winner_app) had been called. The winning application receives a StasisStart event and has full channel control until it calls continue or the channel hangs up.
If no application claims the channel within the timeout, control returns to the dialplan immediately, allowing fallback handling.
This application will set the following channel variables:

variable.name: STASISSTATUS
variable.value: An application claimed the channel and the Stasis session completed without failures.
An application claimed the channel but a failure occurred when executing the Stasis application.
No application claimed the channel within the timeout period.

description.example: ; Broadcast with default timeout (500ms) to all apps ; Channel automatically enters Stasis with the winner exten => _X.,1,StasisBroadcast() same => n,GotoIf($["${STASISSTATUS}"="TIMEOUT"]?no_route) same => n,Hangup() same => n(no_route),Playback(sorry-no-agent) same => n,Hangup()

; Broadcast with custom timeout, app filter, and args for the winner exten => _X.,1,StasisBroadcast(2000,^ivr-.*,sales:priority-high) same => n,GotoIf($["${STASISSTATUS}"="TIMEOUT"]?no_route) same => n,Hangup() same => n(no_route),Playback(sorry-no-agent) same => n,Hangup()

application.name: StatsD
application.synopsis: Allow statistics to be passed to the StatsD server from the dialplan.

parameter.name: metric_type
parameter.para: The metric type to be sent to StatsD. Valid metric types are 'g' for gauge, 'c' for counter, 'ms' for timer, and 's' for sets.

parameter.name: statistic_name
parameter.para: The name of the variable to be sent to StatsD. Statistic names cannot contain the pipe (|) character.

parameter.name: value
parameter.para: The value of the variable to be sent to StatsD. Values must be numeric. Values for gauge and counter metrics can be sent with a '+' or '-' to update a value after the value has been initialized. Only counters can be initialized as negative. Sets can send a string as the value parameter, but the string cannot contain the pipe character.

parameter.name: sample_rate
parameter.para: The value of the sample rate to be sent to StatsD. Sample rates less than or equal to 0 will never be sent and sample rates greater than or equal to 1 will always be sent. Any rate between 1 and 0 will be compared to a randomly generated value, and if it is greater than the random value, it will be sent.

description.para: This dialplan application sends statistics to the StatsD server specified inside of statsd.conf.

application.name: StreamEcho
application.synopsis: Echo media, up to 'N' streams of a type, and DTMF back to the calling party

parameter.name: num
parameter.para: The number of streams of a type to echo back. If '0' is specified then all streams of a type are removed.

parameter.name: type
parameter.para: The media type of the stream(s) to add or remove (in the case of "num" being '0'). This can be set to either "audio" or "video" (default). If "num" is empty (i.e. not specified) then this parameter is ignored.

description.para: If a "num" (the number of streams) is not given then this simply echos back any media or DTMF frames (note, however if '#' is detected then the application exits) read from the calling channel back to itself. This means for any relevant frame read from a particular stream it is written back out to the associated write stream in a one to one fashion.

However if a "num" is specified, and if the calling channel allows it (a new offer is made requesting the allowance of additional streams) then any any media received, like before, is echoed back onto each stream. However, in this case a relevant frame received on a stream of the given "type" is also echoed back out to the other streams of that same type. It should be noted that when operating in this mode only the first stream found of the given "type" is allowed from the original offer. And this first stream found is also the only stream of that "type" granted read (send/receive) capabilities in the new offer whereas the additional ones are set to receive only.

note.para: This does not echo CONTROL, MODEM, or NULL frames.

parameter.name: command
parameter.para: Command to execute

warning.para: Do not use untrusted strings such as CALLERID(num) or CALLERID(name) as part of the command parameters. You risk a command injection attack executing arbitrary commands if the untrusted strings aren't filtered to remove dangerous characters. See function FILTER().

description.para: Executes a command by using system(). If the command fails, the console should report a fallthrough.
Result of execution is returned in the SYSTEMSTATUS channel variable:

variable.name: SYSTEMSTATUS
variable.value: Could not execute the specified command.
Specified command successfully executed.

application.name: BackgroundDetect
application.synopsis: Background a file with talk detect.

parameter.name: sil
parameter.para: If not specified, defaults to 1000.

parameter.name: min
parameter.para: If not specified, defaults to 100.

parameter.name: max
parameter.para: If not specified, defaults to infinity.

parameter.name: analysistime
parameter.para: If not specified, defaults to infinity.

description.para: Plays back filename, waiting for interruption from a given digit (the digit must start the beginning of a valid extension, or it will be ignored). During the playback of the file, audio is monitored in the receive direction, and if a period of non-silence which is greater than min ms yet less than max ms is followed by silence for at least sil ms, which occurs during the first analysistime ms, then the audio playback is aborted and processing jumps to the talk extension, if available.
Perform test server function and write call report. Results stored in /var/log/asterisk/testreports/<testid>-server.txt

parameter.name: testid
parameter.para: An ID to identify this test.

description.para: Executes test client with given testid. Results stored in /var/log/asterisk/testreports/<testid>-client.txt

Requests the remote caller be transferred to a given destination. If TECH (SIP, IAX2, etc) is used, only an incoming call with the same channel technology will be transferred. Note that for SIP, if you transfer before call is setup, a 302 redirect SIP message will be returned to the caller.
The result of the application will be reported in the TRANSFERSTATUS channel variable:

variable.name: TRANSFERSTATUS
variable.value: Transfer succeeded.
Transfer failed.
Transfer unsupported by channel driver.

variable.name: TRANSFERSTATUSPROTOCOL
variable.value: No error.
SIP example - Error result code.

application.name: UserEvent
application.synopsis: Send an arbitrary user-defined event to parties interested in a channel (AMI users and relevant res_stasis applications).

description.para: Sends an arbitrary event to interested parties, with an optional body representing additional arguments. The body may be specified as a , delimited list of key:value pairs.
For AMI, each additional argument will be placed on a new line in the event and the format of the event will be:
Event: UserEvent
UserEvent: <specified event name>
[body]
If no body is specified, only Event and UserEvent headers will be present.
For res_stasis applications, the event will be provided as a JSON blob with additional arguments appearing as keys in the object and the eventname under the eventname key.

manager.name: VoicemailRefresh
manager.synopsis: Tell Asterisk to poll mailboxes for a change

description.para: Normally, MWI indicators are only sent when Asterisk itself changes a mailbox. With external programs that modify the content of a mailbox from outside the application, an option exists called pollmailboxes that will cause voicemail to continually scan all mailboxes on a system for changes. This can cause a large amount of load on a system. This command allows external applications to signal when a particular mailbox has changed, thus permitting external applications to modify mailboxes and MWI to work without introducing considerable CPU load.

If Context is not specified, all mailboxes on the system will be polled for changes. If Context is specified, but Mailbox is omitted, then all mailboxes within Context will be polled. Otherwise, only a single mailbox will be polled for changes.

The VoiceMailMain application will exit if the following DTMF digit is entered as Mailbox or Password, and the extension exists:

enum.para: Jump to the a extension in the current dialplan context.

option.name: s
option.para: Skip playing the initial prompts.

description.para: This application behaves the same way as the Authenticate application, but the passwords are taken from voicemail.conf. If the mailbox is specified, only that mailbox's password will be considered valid. If the mailbox is not specified, the channel variable AUTH_MAILBOX will be set with the authenticated mailbox.
The VMAuthenticate application will exit if the following DTMF digit is entered as Mailbox or Password, and the extension exists:

enum.para: Jump to the a extension in the current dialplan context.

Similar to the Background() application, playback of the recorded name can be interrupted by entering an extension, which will be searched for in the current context.

manager.name: VoicemailRefresh
manager.synopsis: Tell Asterisk to poll mailboxes for a change

description.para: Normally, MWI indicators are only sent when Asterisk itself changes a mailbox. With external programs that modify the content of a mailbox from outside the application, an option exists called pollmailboxes that will cause voicemail to continually scan all mailboxes on a system for changes. This can cause a large amount of load on a system. This command allows external applications to signal when a particular mailbox has changed, thus permitting external applications to modify mailboxes and MWI to work without introducing considerable CPU load.

If Context is not specified, all mailboxes on the system will be polled for changes. If Context is specified, but Mailbox is omitted, then all mailboxes within Context will be polled. Otherwise, only a single mailbox will be polled for changes.
