application.name: WaitForCondition
application.synopsis: Wait (sleep) until the given condition is true.

parameter.name: replacementchar
parameter.para: Specifies the character in the expression used to replace the $ character. This character should not be used anywhere in the expression itself.

parameter.name: expression
parameter.para: A modified logical expression with the $ characters replaced by replacementchar. This is necessary to pass the expression itself into the application, rather than its initial evaluation.

parameter.name: timeout
parameter.para: The maximum amount of time, in seconds, this application should wait for a condition to become true before dialplan execution continues automatically to the next priority. By default, there is no timeout.

parameter.name: interval
parameter.para: The frequency, in seconds, of polling the condition, which can be adjusted depending on how time-sensitive execution needs to be. By default, this is 0.05.

description.para: Waits until expression evaluates to true, checking every interval seconds for up to timeout. Default is evaluate expression every 50 milliseconds with no timeout.

example.title: Wait for condition dialplan variable/function to become 1 for up to 40 seconds, checking every 500ms

description.para: Sets WAITFORCONDITIONSTATUS to one of the following values:

variable.name: WAITFORCONDITIONSTATUS
variable.value: Condition evaluated to true before timeout expired.
Invalid argument.
Timeout elapsed without condition evaluating to true.
Channel hung up before condition became true.

description.para: Returns 0 after waiting at least timeout seconds, and only after the next ring has completed. Returns 0 on success or -1 on hangup.

application.name: WaitForSilence
application.synopsis: Waits for a specified amount of silence.

parameter.name: silencerequired
parameter.para: If not specified, defaults to 1000 milliseconds.

parameter.name: iterations
parameter.para: If not specified, defaults to 1.

parameter.name: timeout
parameter.para: Is specified only to avoid an infinite loop in cases where silence is never achieved.

description.para: Waits for up to silencerequired milliseconds of silence, iterations times. An optional timeout specified the number of seconds to return after, even if we do not receive the specified amount of silence. Use timeout with caution, as it may defeat the purpose of this application, which is to wait indefinitely until silence is detected on the line. This is particularly useful for reverse-911-type call broadcast applications where you need to wait for an answering machine to complete its spiel before playing a message.
Typically you will want to include two or more calls to WaitForSilence when dealing with an answering machine; first waiting for the spiel to finish, then waiting for the beep, etc.

example.title: Wait for half a second of silence, twice
Wait for one second of silence, once
Wait for 300 ms of silence, 3 times, and returns after 10 seconds, even if no silence detected

description.para: Sets the channel variable WAITSTATUS to one of these values:

variable.name: WAITSTATUS
variable.value: if exited with silence detected.
if exited without silence detected after timeout.

application.name: WaitForNoise
application.synopsis: Waits for a specified amount of noise.

parameter.name: noiserequired
parameter.para: If not specified, defaults to 1000 milliseconds.

parameter.name: iterations
parameter.para: If not specified, defaults to 1.

parameter.name: timeout
parameter.para: Is specified only to avoid an infinite loop in cases where silence is never achieved.

description.para: Waits for up to noiserequired milliseconds of noise, iterations times. An optional timeout specified the number of seconds to return after, even if we do not receive the specified amount of noise. Use timeout with caution, as it may defeat the purpose of this application, which is to wait indefinitely until noise is detected on the line.

application.name: WaitUntil
application.synopsis: Wait (sleep) until the current time is the given epoch.

description.para: Waits until the given epoch.
Sets WAITUNTILSTATUS to one of the following values:

variable.name: WAITUNTILSTATUS
variable.value: Wait succeeded.
Invalid argument.
Channel hungup before time elapsed.
Time specified had already past.

description.para: Start a While Loop. Execution will return to this point when EndWhile() is called until expr is no longer true.
Return to the previous called While().
Exits a While() loop, whether or not the conditional has been satisfied.
Returns to the top of the while loop and re-evaluates the conditional.

parameter.name: options
parameter.para: Comma delimited list of options.

option.name: answer
option.para: Causes the line to be answered before playing the tone.

option.name: nocallerid
option.para: Causes Zapateller to only play the tone if there is no callerid information available.

description.para: Generates special information tone to block telemarketers from calling you.
This application will set the following channel variable upon completion:

variable.name: ZAPATELLERSTATUS
variable.para: This will contain the last action accomplished by the Zapateller application. Possible values include:

configObject.name: user_profile
configObject.synopsis: A named profile to apply to specific callers.

description.para: Callers in a ConfBridge have a profile associated with them that determine their options. A configuration section is determined to be a user_profile when the type parameter has a value of user.

configOption.name: type
configOption.synopsis: Define this configuration category as a user profile.

description.para: The type parameter determines how a context in the configuration file is interpreted.

enum.name: user
enum.para: Configure the context as a user_profile

enum.name: bridge
enum.para: Configure the context as a bridge_profile

enum.name: menu
enum.para: Configure the context as a menu

configOption.name: admin
configOption.synopsis: Sets if the user is an admin or not

configOption.name: send_events
configOption.synopsis: Sets if events are send to the user

description.para: If events are enabled for this bridge and this option is set, users will receive events like join, leave, talking, etc. via text messages. For users accessing the bridge via chan_pjsip, this means in-dialog MESSAGE messages. This is most useful for WebRTC participants where the browser application can use the messages to alter the user interface.

configOption.name: echo_events
configOption.synopsis: Sets if events are echoed back to the user that triggered them

description.para: If events are enabled for this user and this option is set, the user will receive events they trigger, talking, mute, etc. If not set, they will not receive their own events.

configOption.name: marked
configOption.synopsis: Sets if this is a marked user or not

configOption.name: startmuted
configOption.synopsis: Sets if all users should start out muted

configOption.name: music_on_hold_when_empty
configOption.synopsis: Play MOH when user is alone or waiting on a marked user

configOption.name: quiet
configOption.synopsis: Silence enter/leave prompts and user intros for this user

configOption.name: hear_own_join_sound
configOption.synopsis: Determines if the user also hears the join sound when they enter a conference

configOption.name: announce_user_count
configOption.synopsis: Sets if the number of users should be announced to the user

configOption.name: announce_user_count_all
configOption.synopsis: Announce user count to all the other users when this user joins

description.para: Sets if the number of users should be announced to all the other users in the conference when this user joins. This option can be either set to 'yes' or a number. When set to a number, the announcement will only occur once the user count is above the specified number.

configOption.name: announce_only_user
configOption.synopsis: Announce to a user when they join an empty conference

configOption.name: wait_marked
configOption.synopsis: Sets if the user must wait for a marked user to enter before joining a conference

configOption.name: end_marked
configOption.synopsis: Kick the user from the conference when the last marked user leaves

configOption.name: end_marked_any
configOption.synopsis: Kick the user from the conference when any marked user leaves

configOption.name: talk_detection_events
configOption.synopsis: Set whether or not notifications of when a user begins and ends talking should be sent out as events over AMI

configOption.name: dtmf_passthrough
configOption.synopsis: Sets whether or not DTMF should pass through the conference

configOption.name: announce_join_leave
configOption.synopsis: Prompt user for their name when joining a conference and play it to the conference when they enter

configOption.name: announce_join_leave_review
configOption.synopsis: Prompt user for their name when joining a conference and play it to the conference when they enter. The user will be asked to review the recording of their name before entering the conference.

configOption.name: pin
configOption.synopsis: Sets a PIN the user must enter before joining the conference

configOption.name: music_on_hold_class
configOption.synopsis: The MOH class to use for this user

configOption.name: announcement
configOption.synopsis: Sound file to play to the user when they join a conference

configOption.name: denoise
configOption.synopsis: Apply a denoise filter to the audio before mixing

description.para: Sets whether or not a denoise filter should be applied to the audio before mixing or not. Off by default. Requires codec_speex to be built and installed. Do not confuse this option with drop_silence. Denoise is useful if there is a lot of background noise for a user as it attempts to remove the noise while preserving the speech. This option does NOT remove silence from being mixed into the conference and does come at the cost of a slight performance hit.

configOption.name: dsp_drop_silence
configOption.synopsis: Drop what Asterisk detects as silence from audio sent to the bridge

description.para: This option drops what Asterisk detects as silence from entering into the bridge. Enabling this option will drastically improve performance and help remove the buildup of background noise from the conference. Highly recommended for large conferences due to its performance enhancements.

configOption.name: dsp_silence_threshold
configOption.synopsis: The number of milliseconds of silence necessary to declare talking stopped.

description.para: The time in milliseconds of sound falling below the dsp_talking_threshold option when a user is considered to stop talking. This value affects several operations and should not be changed unless the impact on call quality is fully understood.
What this value affects internally:

1. When talk detection AMI events are enabled, this value determines when the user has stopped talking after a period of talking. If this value is set too low AMI events indicating the user has stopped talking may get falsely sent out when the user briefly pauses during mid sentence.

2. The drop_silence option depends on this value to determine when the user's audio should begin to be dropped from the conference bridge after the user stops talking. If this value is set too low the user's audio stream may sound choppy to the other participants. This is caused by the user transitioning constantly from silence to talking during mid sentence.
The best way to approach this option is to set it slightly above the maximum amount of milliseconds of silence a user may generate during natural speech.
Valid values are 1 through 2^31.

configOption.name: dsp_talking_threshold
configOption.synopsis: Average magnitude threshold to determine talking.

description.para: The minimum average magnitude per sample in a frame for the DSP to consider talking/noise present. A value below this level is considered silence. This value affects several operations and should not be changed unless the impact on call quality is fully understood.
What this value affects internally:
1. Audio is only mixed out of a user's incoming audio stream if talking is detected. If this value is set too high the user will hear himself talking.

2. When talk detection AMI events are enabled, this value determines when talking has begun which results in an AMI event to fire. If this value is set too low AMI events may be falsely triggered by variants in room noise.

3. The drop_silence option depends on this value to determine when the user's audio should be mixed into the bridge after periods of silence. If this value is too high the user's speech will get discarded as they will be considered silent.
Valid values are 1 through 2^15.

configOption.name: jitterbuffer
configOption.synopsis: Place a jitter buffer on the user's audio stream before audio mixing is performed

description.para: Enabling this option places a jitterbuffer on the user's audio stream before audio mixing is performed. This is highly recommended but will add a slight delay to the audio. This option is using the JITTERBUFFER dialplan function's default adaptive jitterbuffer. For a more fine tuned jitterbuffer, disable this option and use the JITTERBUFFER dialplan function on the user before entering the ConfBridge application.

configOption.name: template
configOption.synopsis: When using the CONFBRIDGE dialplan function, use a user profile as a template for creating a new temporary profile

configOption.name: timeout
configOption.synopsis: Kick the user out of the conference after this many seconds. 0 means there is no timeout for the user.

configOption.name: text_messaging
configOption.synopsis: Sets if text messages are sent to the user.

description.para: If text messaging is enabled for this user then text messages will be sent to it. These may be events or from other participants in the conference bridge. If disabled then no text messages are sent to the user.

configOption.name: answer_channel
configOption.synopsis: Sets if a user's channel should be answered if currently unanswered.

configObject.name: bridge_profile
configObject.synopsis: A named profile to apply to specific bridges.

description.para: ConfBridge bridges have a profile associated with them that determine their options. A configuration section is determined to be a bridge_profile when the type parameter has a value of bridge.

configOption.name: type
configOption.synopsis: Define this configuration category as a bridge profile

description.para: The type parameter determines how a context in the configuration file is interpreted.

enum.name: user
enum.para: Configure the context as a user_profile

enum.name: bridge
enum.para: Configure the context as a bridge_profile

enum.name: menu
enum.para: Configure the context as a menu

configOption.name: jitterbuffer
configOption.synopsis: Place a jitter buffer on the conference's audio stream

configOption.name: internal_sample_rate
configOption.synopsis: Set the internal native sample rate for mixing the conference

description.para: Sets the internal native sample rate the conference is mixed at. This is set to automatically adjust the sample rate to the best quality by default. Other values can be anything from 8000-192000. If a sample rate is set that Asterisk does not support, the closest sample rate Asterisk does support to the one requested will be used.

configOption.name: maximum_sample_rate
configOption.synopsis: Set the maximum native sample rate for mixing the conference

description.para: Sets the maximum native sample rate the conference is mixed at. This is set to not have a maximum by default. If a sample rate is specified, though, the native sample rate will never exceed it.

configOption.name: language
configOption.synopsis: The language used for announcements to the conference.

description.para: By default, announcements to a conference use English. Which means the prompts played to all users within the conference will be English. By changing the language of a bridge, this will change the language of the prompts played to all users.

configOption.name: mixing_interval
configOption.synopsis: Sets the internal mixing interval in milliseconds for the bridge

description.para: Sets the internal mixing interval in milliseconds for the bridge. This number reflects how tight or loose the mixing will be for the conference. In order to improve performance a larger mixing interval such as 40ms may be chosen. Using a larger mixing interval comes at the cost of introducing larger amounts of delay into the bridge. Valid values here are 10, 20, 40, or 80.

configOption.name: binaural_active
configOption.synopsis: If true binaural conferencing with stereo audio is active

description.para: Activates binaural mixing for a conference bridge. Binaural features are disabled by default.

configOption.name: record_conference
configOption.synopsis: Record the conference starting with the first active user's entrance and ending with the last active user's exit

description.para: Records the conference call starting when the first user enters the room, and ending when the last user exits the room. The default recorded filename is 'confbridge-${name of conference bridge}-${start time}.wav' and the default format is 8khz slinear. This file will be located in the configured monitoring directory in asterisk.conf.

configOption.name: record_file
configOption.synopsis: The filename of the conference recording

description.para: When record_conference is set to yes, the specific name of the record file can be set using this option. Note that since multiple conferences may use the same bridge profile, this may cause issues depending on the configuration. It is recommended to only use this option dynamically with the CONFBRIDGE() dialplan function. This allows the record name to be specified and a unique name to be chosen. By default, the record_file is stored in Asterisk's spool/monitor directory with a unique filename starting with the 'confbridge' prefix.

configOption.name: record_file_append
configOption.synopsis: Append to record file when starting/stopping on same conference recording

description.para: When record_file_append is set to yes, stopping and starting recording on a conference adds the new portion to end of current record_file. When this is set to no, a new record_file is generated every time you start then stop recording on a conference.

configOption.name: record_file_timestamp
configOption.synopsis: Append the start time to the record_file name so that it is unique.

description.para: When record_file_timestamp is set to yes, the start time is appended to record_file so that the filename is unique. This allows you to specify a record_file but not overwrite existing recordings.

configOption.name: record_options
configOption.synopsis: Pass additional options to MixMonitor when recording

description.para: Pass additional options to MixMonitor when record_conference is set to yes. See MixMonitor for available options.

configOption.name: record_command
configOption.synopsis: Execute a command after recording ends

description.para: Executes the specified command when recording ends. Any strings matching ^{X} will be unescaped to X. All variables will be evaluated at the time ConfBridge is called.

configOption.name: regcontext
configOption.synopsis: The name of the context into which to register the name of the conference bridge as NoOP() at priority 1

description.para: When set this will cause the name of the created conference to be registered into the named context at priority 1 with an operation of NoOP(). This can then be used in other parts of the dialplan to test for the existence of a specific conference bridge. You should be aware that there are potential races between testing for the existence of a bridge, and taking action upon that information, consider for example two callers executing the check simultaneously, and then taking special action as "first caller" into the bridge. The same for exiting, directly after the check the bridge can be destroyed before the new caller enters (creating a new bridge), for example, and the "first member" actions could thus be missed.

configOption.name: video_mode
configOption.synopsis: Sets how confbridge handles video distribution to the conference participants

description.para: Sets how confbridge handles video distribution to the conference participants. Note that participants wanting to view and be the source of a video feed MUST be sharing the same video codec. Also, using video in conjunction with with the jitterbuffer currently results in the audio being slightly out of sync with the video. This is a result of the jitterbuffer only working on the audio stream. It is recommended to disable the jitterbuffer when video is used.

enum.name: none
enum.para: No video sources are set by default in the conference. It is still possible for a user to be set as a video source via AMI or DTMF action at any time.

enum.name: follow_talker
enum.para: The video feed will follow whoever is talking and providing video.

enum.name: last_marked
enum.para: The last marked user to join the conference with video capabilities will be the single source of video distributed to all participants. If multiple marked users are capable of video, the last one to join is always the source, when that user leaves it goes to the one who joined before them.

enum.name: first_marked
enum.para: The first marked user to join the conference with video capabilities is the single source of video distribution among all participants. If that user leaves, the marked user to join after them becomes the source.

enum.name: sfu
enum.para: Selective Forwarding Unit - Sets multi-stream operation for a multi-party video conference.

configOption.name: max_members
configOption.synopsis: Limit the maximum number of participants for a single conference

description.para: This option limits the number of participants for a single conference to a specific number. By default conferences have no participant limit. After the limit is reached, the conference will be locked until someone leaves. Note however that an Admin user will always be allowed to join the conference regardless if this limit is reached or not.

configOption.name: sound_
configOption.synopsis: Override the various conference bridge sound files

description.para: All sounds in the conference are customizable using the bridge profile options below. Simply state the option followed by the filename or full path of the filename after the option. Example: sound_had_joined=conf-hasjoin This will play the conf-hasjoin sound file found in the sounds directory when announcing someone's name is joining the conference.

enum.name: sound_join
enum.para: The sound played to everyone when someone enters the conference.

enum.name: sound_leave
enum.para: The sound played to everyone when someone leaves the conference.

enum.name: sound_has_joined
enum.para: The sound played before announcing someone's name has joined the conference. This is used for user intros. Example "_____ has joined the conference"

enum.name: sound_has_left
enum.para: The sound played when announcing someone's name has left the conference. This is used for user intros. Example "_____ has left the conference"

enum.name: sound_kicked
enum.para: The sound played to a user who has been kicked from the conference.

enum.name: sound_muted
enum.para: The sound played when the mute option it toggled on.

enum.name: sound_unmuted
enum.para: The sound played when the mute option it toggled off.

enum.name: sound_binaural_on
enum.para: The sound played when binaural audio is turned on.

enum.name: sound_binaural_off
enum.para: The sound played when the binaural audio is turned off.

enum.name: sound_only_person
enum.para: The sound played when the user is the only person in the conference.

enum.name: sound_only_one
enum.para: The sound played to a user when there is only one other person is in the conference.

enum.name: sound_there_are
enum.para: The sound played when announcing how many users there are in a conference.

enum.name: sound_other_in_party
enum.para: This file is used in conjunction with sound_there_are when announcing how many users there are in the conference. The sounds are stringed together like this. "sound_there_are" ${number of participants} "sound_other_in_party"

enum.name: sound_place_into_conference
enum.para: The sound played when someone is placed into the conference after waiting for a marked user.

enum.name: sound_wait_for_leader
enum.para: The sound played when a user is placed into a conference that can not start until a marked user enters.

enum.name: sound_leader_has_left
enum.para: The sound played when the last marked user leaves the conference.

enum.name: sound_get_pin
enum.para: The sound played when prompting for a conference pin number.

enum.name: sound_invalid_pin
enum.para: The sound played when an invalid pin is entered too many times.

enum.name: sound_locked
enum.para: The sound played to a user trying to join a locked conference.

enum.name: sound_locked_now
enum.para: The sound played to an admin after toggling the conference to locked mode.

enum.name: sound_unlocked_now
enum.para: The sound played to an admin after toggling the conference to unlocked mode.

enum.name: sound_error_menu
enum.para: The sound played when an invalid menu option is entered.

configOption.name: video_update_discard
configOption.synopsis: Sets the amount of time in milliseconds after sending a video update to discard subsequent video updates

description.para: Sets the amount of time in milliseconds after sending a video update request that subsequent video updates should be discarded. This means that if we send a video update we will discard any other video update requests until after the configured amount of time has elapsed. This prevents flooding of video update requests from clients.

configOption.name: remb_send_interval
configOption.synopsis: Sets the interval in milliseconds that a combined REMB frame will be sent to video sources

description.para: Sets the interval in milliseconds that a combined REMB frame will be sent to video sources. This is done by taking all REMB frames that have been received since the last REMB frame was sent, making a combined value, and sending it to the source. A REMB frame contains receiver estimated maximum bitrate information. By creating a combined REMB frame the sender of video can be influenced on the bitrate they choose, allowing better quality for all receivers.

configOption.name: remb_behavior
configOption.synopsis: Sets how REMB reports are generated from multiple sources

description.para: Sets how REMB reports are combined from multiple sources to form one. A REMB report consists of information about the receiver estimated maximum bitrate. As a source stream may be forwarded to multiple receivers the reports must be combined into a single one which is sent to the sender.

enum.name: average
enum.para: The average of all estimated maximum bitrates is taken and sent to the sender.

enum.name: lowest
enum.para: The lowest estimated maximum bitrate is forwarded to the sender.

enum.name: highest
enum.para: The highest estimated maximum bitrate is forwarded to the sender.

enum.name: average_all
enum.para: The average of all estimated maximum bitrates is taken from all receivers in the bridge and a single value is sent to each sender.

enum.name: lowest_all
enum.para: The lowest estimated maximum bitrate of all receivers in the bridge is taken and sent to each sender.

enum.name: highest_all
enum.para: The highest estimated maximum bitrate of all receivers in the bridge is taken and sent to each sender.

enum.name: force
enum.para: The bitrate configured in remb_estimated_bitrate is sent to each sender.

configOption.name: remb_estimated_bitrate
configOption.synopsis: Sets the estimated bitrate sent to each participant in REMB reports

description.para: When remb_behavior is set to force, this options sets the estimated bitrate (in bits per second) sent to each participant in REMB reports.

configOption.name: enable_events
configOption.synopsis: Enables events for this bridge

description.para: If enabled, recipients who joined the bridge via a channel driver that supports Enhanced Messaging (currently only chan_pjsip) will receive in-dialog messages containing a JSON body describing the event. The Content-Type header will be text/x-ast-confbridge-event. This feature must also be enabled in user profiles.

configOption.name: template
configOption.synopsis: When using the CONFBRIDGE dialplan function, use a bridge profile as a template for creating a new temporary profile

description.para: Conference users, as defined by a conf_user, can have a DTMF menu assigned to their profile when they enter the ConfBridge application.

configOption.name: type
configOption.synopsis: Define this configuration category as a menu

description.para: The type parameter determines how a context in the configuration file is interpreted.

enum.name: user
enum.para: Configure the context as a user_profile

enum.name: bridge
enum.para: Configure the context as a bridge_profile

enum.name: menu
enum.para: Configure the context as a menu

configOption.name: template
configOption.synopsis: When using the CONFBRIDGE dialplan function, use a menu profile as a template for creating a new temporary profile

configOption.name: ^[0-9A-D*#]+$
configOption.synopsis: DTMF sequences to assign various confbridge actions to

description.para: The ConfBridge application also has the ability to apply custom DTMF menus to each channel using the application. Like the User and Bridge profiles a menu is passed in to ConfBridge as an argument in the dialplan.
Below is a list of menu actions that can be assigned to a DTMF sequence.

note.para: To have the first DTMF digit in a sequence be the '#' character, you need to escape it. If it is not escaped then normal config file processing will think it is a directive like #include. For example: The mute setting is toggled when #1 is pressed.

A single DTMF sequence can have multiple actions associated with it. This is accomplished by stringing the actions together and using a , as the delimiter. Example: Both listening and talking volume is reset when 5 is pressed. 5=reset_talking_volume, reset_listening_volume

enum.name: playback(filename&filename2&...)
enum.para: playback will play back an audio file to a channel and then immediately return to the conference. This file can not be interrupted by DTMF. Multiple files can be chained together using the & character.

enum.name: playback_and_continue(filename&filename2&...)
enum.para: playback_and_continue will play back a prompt while continuing to collect the dtmf sequence. This is useful when using a menu prompt that describes all the menu options. Note however that any DTMF during this action will terminate the prompts playback. Prompt files can be chained together using the & character as a delimiter.

enum.name: toggle_mute
enum.para: Toggle turning on and off mute. Mute will make the user silent to everyone else, but the user will still be able to listen in.

enum.name: toggle_binaural
enum.para: Toggle turning on and off binaural audio processing.

enum.name: no_op
enum.para: This action does nothing (No Operation). Its only real purpose exists for being able to reserve a sequence in the config as a menu exit sequence.

enum.name: decrease_listening_volume
enum.para: Decreases the channel's listening volume.

enum.name: increase_listening_volume
enum.para: Increases the channel's listening volume.

enum.name: reset_listening_volume
enum.para: Reset channel's listening volume to default level.

enum.name: decrease_talking_volume
enum.para: Decreases the channel's talking volume.

enum.name: increase_talking_volume
enum.para: Increases the channel's talking volume.

enum.name: reset_talking_volume
enum.para: Reset channel's talking volume to default level.

enum.name: dialplan_exec(context,exten,priority)
enum.para: The dialplan_exec action allows a user to escape from the conference and execute commands in the dialplan. Once the dialplan exits the user will be put back into the conference. The possibilities are endless!

enum.name: leave_conference
enum.para: This action allows a user to exit the conference and continue execution in the dialplan.

enum.name: admin_kick_last
enum.para: This action allows an Admin to kick the last participant from the conference. This action will only work for admins which allows a single menu to be used for both users and admins.

enum.name: admin_toggle_conference_lock
enum.para: This action allows an Admin to toggle locking and unlocking the conference. Non admins can not use this action even if it is in their menu.

enum.name: set_as_single_video_src
enum.para: This action allows any user to set themselves as the single video source distributed to all participants. This will make the video feed stick to them regardless of what the video_mode is set to.

enum.name: release_as_single_video_src
enum.para: This action allows a user to release themselves as the video source. If video_mode is not set to none this action will result in the conference returning to whatever video mode the bridge profile is using.

Note that this action will have no effect if the user is not currently the video source. Also, the user is not guaranteed by using this action that they will not become the video source again. The bridge will return to whatever operation the video_mode option is set to upon release of the video src.

enum.name: admin_toggle_mute_participants
enum.para: This action allows an administrator to toggle the mute state for all non-admins within a conference. All admin users are unaffected by this option. Note that all users, regardless of their admin status, are notified that the conference is muted.

enum.name: participant_count
enum.para: This action plays back the number of participants currently in a conference

managerEventInstance.synopsis: Raised when a CDR is generated.

parameter.name: AccountCode
parameter.para: The account code of the Party A channel.

parameter.name: Source
parameter.para: The Caller ID number associated with the Party A in the CDR.

parameter.name: Destination
parameter.para: The dialplan extension the Party A was executing.

parameter.name: DestinationContext
parameter.para: The dialplan context the Party A was executing.

parameter.name: CallerID
parameter.para: The Caller ID name associated with the Party A in the CDR.

parameter.name: Channel
parameter.para: The channel name of the Party A.

parameter.name: DestinationChannel
parameter.para: The channel name of the Party B.

parameter.name: LastApplication
parameter.para: The last dialplan application the Party A executed.

parameter.name: LastData
parameter.para: The parameters passed to the last dialplan application the Party A executed.

parameter.name: StartTime
parameter.para: The time the CDR was created.

parameter.name: AnswerTime
parameter.para: The earliest of either the time when Party A answered, or the start time of this CDR.

parameter.name: EndTime
parameter.para: The time when the CDR was finished. This occurs when the Party A hangs up or when the bridge between Party A and Party B is broken.

parameter.name: Duration
parameter.para: The time, in seconds, of EndTime - StartTime.

parameter.name: BillableSeconds
parameter.para: The time, in seconds, of AnswerTime - StartTime.

parameter.name: Disposition
parameter.para: The final known disposition of the CDR.

enum.name: NO ANSWER
enum.para: The channel was not answered. This is the default disposition.

enum.name: FAILED
enum.para: The channel attempted to dial but the call failed.

note.para: The congestion setting in cdr.conf can result in the AST_CAUSE_CONGESTION hang up cause or the CONGESTION dial status to map to this disposition.

enum.name: BUSY
enum.para: The channel attempted to dial but the remote party was busy.

enum.name: ANSWERED
enum.para: The channel was answered. The hang up cause will no longer impact the disposition of the CDR.

enum.name: CONGESTION
enum.para: The channel attempted to dial but the remote party was congested.

parameter.name: AMAFlags
parameter.para: A flag that informs a billing system how to treat the CDR.

enum.name: OMIT
enum.para: This CDR should be ignored.

enum.name: BILLING
enum.para: This CDR contains valid billing data.

enum.name: DOCUMENTATION
enum.para: This CDR is for documentation purposes.

parameter.name: UniqueID
parameter.para: A unique identifier for the Party A channel.

parameter.name: UserField
parameter.para: A user defined field set on the channels. If set on both the Party A and Party B channel, the userfields of both are concatenated and separated by a ;.

description.para: The Cdr event is only raised when the cdr_manager backend is loaded and registered with the CDR engine.

note.para: This event can contain additional fields depending on the configuration provided by cdr_manager.conf.

managerEventInstance.synopsis: Raised when a Channel Event Log is generated for a channel.

parameter.name: EventName
parameter.para: The name of the CEL event being raised. This can include both the system defined CEL events, as well as user defined events.

note.para: All events listed here may not be raised, depending on the configuration in cel.conf.

enum.name: CHAN_START
enum.para: A channel was created.

enum.name: CHAN_END
enum.para: A channel was terminated.

enum.name: ANSWER
enum.para: A channel answered.

enum.name: HANGUP
enum.para: A channel was hung up.

enum.name: BRIDGE_ENTER
enum.para: A channel entered a bridge.

enum.name: BRIDGE_EXIT
enum.para: A channel left a bridge.

enum.name: APP_START
enum.para: A channel entered into a tracked application.

enum.name: APP_END
enum.para: A channel left a tracked application.

enum.name: PARK_START
enum.para: A channel was parked.

enum.name: PARK_END
enum.para: A channel was unparked.

enum.name: BLINDTRANSFER
enum.para: A channel initiated a blind transfer.

enum.name: ATTENDEDTRANSFER
enum.para: A channel initiated an attended transfer.

enum.name: PICKUP
enum.para: A channel initated a call pickup.

enum.name: FORWARD
enum.para: A channel is being forwarded to another destination.

enum.name: LINKEDID_END
enum.para: The linked ID associated with this channel is being retired.

enum.name: LOCAL_OPTIMIZE_BEGIN
enum.para: A Local channel optimization has begun.

enum.name: LOCAL_OPTIMIZE
enum.para: A Local channel optimization has occurred.

enum.name: STREAM_BEGIN
enum.para: A stream started playing: it can be a standalone sound file playing back, or a music-on-hold class started.

enum.name: STREAM_END
enum.para: A playing stream ended.

enum.name: DTMF
enum.para: A DTMF digit was processed: these events are dispatched at the end, when the button is released and the duration is present in the extra field

enum.name: USER_DEFINED
enum.para: A user defined type.

note.para: This event is only present if show_user_defined in cel.conf is True. Otherwise, the user defined event will be placed directly in the EventName field.

parameter.name: AccountCode
parameter.para: The channel's account code.

parameter.name: CallerIDnum
parameter.para: The Caller ID number.

parameter.name: CallerIDname
parameter.para: The Caller ID name.

parameter.name: CallerIDani
parameter.para: The Caller ID Automatic Number Identification.

parameter.name: CallerIDrdnis
parameter.para: The Caller ID Redirected Dialed Number Identification Service.

parameter.name: CallerIDdnid
parameter.para: The Caller ID Dialed Number Identifier.

parameter.name: Exten
parameter.para: The dialplan extension the channel is currently executing in.

parameter.name: Context
parameter.para: The dialplan context the channel is currently executing in.

parameter.name: Application
parameter.para: The dialplan application the channel is currently executing.

parameter.name: AppData
parameter.para: The arguments passed to the dialplan Application.

parameter.name: EventTime
parameter.para: The time the CEL event occurred.

parameter.name: AMAFlags
parameter.para: A flag that informs a billing system how to treat the CEL.

enum.name: OMIT
enum.para: This event should be ignored.

enum.name: BILLING
enum.para: This event contains valid billing data.

enum.name: DOCUMENTATION
enum.para: This event is for documentation purposes.

parameter.name: UniqueID
parameter.para: The unique ID of the channel.

parameter.name: LinkedID
parameter.para: The linked ID of the channel, which ties this event to other related channel's events.

parameter.name: UserField
parameter.para: A user defined field set on a channel, containing arbitrary application specific data.

parameter.name: Peer
parameter.para: If this channel is in a bridge, the channel that it is in a bridge with.

parameter.name: PeerAccount
parameter.para: If this channel is in a bridge, the accountcode of the channel it is in a bridge with.

parameter.name: Extra
parameter.para: Some events will have event specific data that accompanies the CEL record. This extra data is JSON encoded, and is dependent on the event in question.

variable.name: CALL_QUALIFIER
variable.para: This is a special Caller ID-related variable that can be used to enable sending the Call Qualifier parameter in MDMF (Multiple Data Message Format) Caller ID spills.
This variable is not automatically set by Asterisk. You are responsible for setting it if/when needed.
Supporting Caller ID units will display the LDC (Long Distance Call) indicator when they receive this parameter.
For incoming calls on FXO ports, if the Call Qualifier parameter is received, this variable will also be set to 1.
This option must be used with a channel driver that allows Asterisk to generate the Caller ID spill, which currently only includes chan_dahdi.

option.name: f
option.para: Returns billsec or duration fields as floating point values.

option.name: u
option.para: Retrieves the raw, unprocessed value.

For example, 'start', 'answer', and 'end' will be retrieved as epoch values, when the u option is passed, but formatted as YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS otherwise. Similarly, disposition and amaflags will return their raw integral values.

description.para: All of the CDR field names are read-only, except for accountcode, userfield, and amaflags. You may, however, supply a name not on the above list, and create your own variable, whose value can be changed with this function, and this variable will be stored on the CDR.

note.para: CDRs can only be modified before the bridge between two channels is torn down. For example, CDRs may not be modified after the Dial application has returned.

function.name: CHANNELS
function.synopsis: Gets the list of channels, optionally filtering by a regular expression.

description.para: Gets the list of channels, optionally filtering by a regular_expression. If no argument is provided, all known channels are returned. The regular_expression must correspond to the POSIX.2 specification, as shown in regex(7). The list returned will be space-delimited.

description.para: Returns 1 if the channel name_or_uid exists, 0 if not.

function.name: MASTER_CHANNEL
function.synopsis: Gets or sets variables on the master channel

description.para: Allows access to the oldest channel associated with the current channel if it still exists. If the channel is the master channel or the master channel no longer exists then access local channel variables instead. In other words, the master channel is the channel identified by the channel's linkedid.

function.name: CHANNEL
function.synopsis: Gets/sets various pieces of information about the channel.

parameter.name: item
parameter.para: Standard items (provided by all channel technologies) are:

enum.name: amaflags
enum.para: R/W the Automatic Message Accounting (AMA) flags on the channel. When read from a channel, the integer value will always be returned. When written to a channel, both the string format or integer value is accepted.

enum.name: accountcode
enum.para: R/W the channel's account code.

enum.name: adsicpe
enum.para: R/W The channel's support for ADSI (Analog Display Services Interface) CPE.

enum.name: audioreadformat
enum.para: R/O format currently being read.

enum.name: audionativeformat
enum.para: R/O format used natively for audio.

enum.name: audiowriteformat
enum.para: R/O format currently being written.

enum.name: dtmf_features
enum.para: R/W The channel's DTMF bridge features. May include one or more of 'T' 'K' 'H' 'W' and 'X' in a similar manner to options in the Dial application. When setting it, the features string must be all upper case.

enum.name: callgroup
enum.para: R/W numeric call pickup groups that this channel is a member.

enum.name: pickupgroup
enum.para: R/W numeric call pickup groups this channel can pickup.

enum.name: namedcallgroup
enum.para: R/W named call pickup groups that this channel is a member.

enum.name: namedpickupgroup
enum.para: R/W named call pickup groups this channel can pickup.

enum.name: channeltype
enum.para: R/O technology used for channel.

enum.name: checkhangup
enum.para: R/O Whether the channel is hanging up (1/0)

enum.name: digitdetect
enum.para: R/W Enable or disable DTMF detection on channel drivers that support it.
If set on a DAHDI channel, this will only disable DTMF detection, not pulse dialing detection. To disable pulse dialing, use the dialmode option.
On DAHDI channels, this will disable DSP if it is not needed for anything else. This will prevent DTMF detection regardless of the dialmode setting.

enum.name: faxdetect
enum.para: R/W Enable or disable fax detection on channel drivers that support it.

enum.name: after_bridge_goto
enum.para: R/W the parseable goto string indicating where the channel is expected to return to in the PBX after exiting the next bridge it joins on the condition that it doesn't hang up. The parseable goto string uses the same syntax as the Goto application.

enum.name: hangup_handler_pop
enum.para: W/O Replace the most recently added hangup handler with a new hangup handler on the channel if supplied. The assigned string is passed to the Gosub application when the channel is hung up. Any optionally omitted context and exten are supplied by the channel pushing the handler before it is pushed.

enum.name: hangup_handler_push
enum.para: W/O Push a hangup handler onto the channel hangup handler stack. The assigned string is passed to the Gosub application when the channel is hung up. Any optionally omitted context and exten are supplied by the channel pushing the handler before it is pushed.

enum.name: hangup_handler_wipe
enum.para: W/O Wipe the entire hangup handler stack and replace with a new hangup handler on the channel if supplied. The assigned string is passed to the Gosub application when the channel is hung up. Any optionally omitted context and exten are supplied by the channel pushing the handler before it is pushed.

enum.name: onhold
enum.para: R/O Whether or not the channel is onhold. (1/0)

enum.name: language
enum.para: R/W language for sounds played.

enum.name: musicclass
enum.para: R/W class (from musiconhold.conf) for hold music.

enum.name: name
enum.para: The name of the channel

enum.name: parkinglot
enum.para: R/W parkinglot for parking.

enum.name: relaxdtmf
enum.para: W/O Enable or disable relaxed DTMF detection for channel drivers that support it, overriding any setting previously defaulted by the channel driver.

enum.name: rxgain
enum.para: R/W set rxgain level on channel drivers that support it.

enum.name: secure_bridge_signaling
enum.para: Whether or not channels bridged to this channel require secure signaling (1/0)

enum.name: secure_bridge_media
enum.para: Whether or not channels bridged to this channel require secure media (1/0)

enum.name: state
enum.para: R/O state of the channel

enum.name: tdd
enum.para: R/W Enable or disable TDD mode on channel drivers that support it.
When reading this option, 1 indicates TDD mode enabled, 0 indicates TDD mode disabled, and mate indicates TDD mate mode.

enum.name: tonezone
enum.para: R/W zone for indications played

enum.name: transfercapability
enum.para: R/W ISDN Transfer Capability, one of:

enum.name: txgain
enum.para: R/W set txgain level on channel drivers that support it.

enum.name: videonativeformat
enum.para: R/O format used natively for video

enum.name: hangupsource
enum.para: R/W returns the channel responsible for hangup.

enum.name: appname
enum.para: R/O returns the internal application name.

enum.name: appdata
enum.para: R/O returns the application data if available.

enum.name: exten
enum.para: R/O returns the extension for an outbound channel.

enum.name: context
enum.para: R/O returns the context for an outbound channel.

enum.name: lastexten
enum.para: R/O returns the last unique extension for an outbound channel.

enum.name: lastcontext
enum.para: R/O returns the last unique context for an outbound channel.

enum.name: channame
enum.para: R/O returns the channel name for an outbound channel.

enum.name: uniqueid
enum.para: R/O returns the channel uniqueid.

enum.name: linkedid
enum.para: R/O returns the linkedid if available, otherwise returns the uniqueid.

enum.name: tenantid
enum.para: R/W The channel tenantid.

enum.name: max_forwards
enum.para: R/W The maximum number of forwards allowed.

enum.name: callid
enum.para: R/O Call identifier log tag associated with the channel e.g., [C-00000000].

description.para: Gets/sets various pieces of information about the channel, additional item may be available from the channel driver; see its documentation for details. Any item requested that is not available on the current channel will return an empty string.
description.example:
; Push a hangup handler subroutine existing at dialplan ; location default,s,1 onto the current channel same => n,Set(CHANNEL(hangup_handler_push)=default,s,1)
; Set the current tonezone to Germany (de) same => n,Set(CHANNEL(tonezone)=de)
; Set the allowed maximum number of forwarding attempts same => n,Set(CHANNEL(max_forwards)=10)
; If this channel is ejected from its next bridge, and if ; the channel is not hung up, begin executing dialplan at ; location default,after-bridge,1 same => n,Set(CHANNEL(after_bridge_goto)=default,after-bridge,1)
; Log the current state of the channel same => n,Log(NOTICE, This channel is: ${CHANNEL(state)})
description.para: The following channel variables are available as special built-in dialplan channel variables. These variables cannot be set or modified and are read-only.

variable.name: CALLINGPRES
variable.para: Caller ID presentation for incoming calls (PRI channels)

variable.name: CALLINGANI2
variable.para: Caller ANI2 (PRI channels)

variable.name: CALLINGTON
variable.para: Caller Type of Number (PRI channels)

variable.name: CALLINGTNS
variable.para: Transit Network Selector (PRI channels)

variable.name: EXTEN
variable.para: Current extension

variable.name: CONTEXT
variable.para: Current context

variable.name: PRIORITY
variable.para: Current priority

variable.name: CHANNEL
variable.para: Current channel name

variable.name: UNIQUEID
variable.para: Current call unique identifier

variable.name: HANGUPCAUSE
variable.para: Asterisk cause of hangup (inbound/outbound)

function.name: AST_CONFIG
function.synopsis: Retrieve a variable from a configuration file.

parameter.name: index
parameter.para: If there are multiple variables with the same name, you can specify 0 for the first item (default), -1 for the last item, or any other number for that specific item. -1 is useful when the variable is derived from a template and you want the effective value (the last occurrence), not the value from the template (the first occurrence).

description.para: This function reads a variable from an Asterisk configuration file.

function.name: CURL
function.synopsis: Retrieve content from a remote web or ftp server

parameter.name: url
parameter.para: The full URL for the resource to retrieve.

parameter.name: post-data
parameter.para: If specified, an HTTP POST will be performed with the content of post-data, instead of an HTTP GET (default).

description.para: When this function is read, a HTTP GET (by default) will be used to retrieve the contents of the provided url. The contents are returned as the result of the function.
When this function is written to, a HTTP GET will be used to retrieve the contents of the provided url. The value written to the function specifies the destination file of the cURL'd resource.

note.para: If live_dangerously in asterisk.conf is set to no, this function can only be written to from the dialplan, and not directly from external protocols. Read operations are unaffected.

function.name: CURLOPT
function.synopsis: Sets various options for future invocations of CURL.

enum.name: cookie
enum.para: A cookie to send with the request. Multiple cookies are supported.

enum.name: conntimeout
enum.para: Number of seconds to wait for a connection to succeed

enum.name: dnstimeout
enum.para: Number of seconds to wait for DNS to be resolved

enum.name: followlocation
enum.para: Whether or not to follow HTTP 3xx redirects (boolean)

enum.name: ftptext
enum.para: For FTP URIs, force a text transfer (boolean)

enum.name: ftptimeout
enum.para: For FTP URIs, number of seconds to wait for a server response

enum.name: header
enum.para: Include header information in the result (boolean)

enum.name: httpauth
enum.para: Type of authentication method to use. The default is Basic Authentication.
Multiple values can be specified to enable multiple authentication methods. To do so, invoke CURLOPT once using comma-separated values.

enum.name: httpheader
enum.para: Add HTTP header. Multiple calls add multiple headers. Setting of any header will remove the default "Content-Type application/x-www-form-urlencoded"

enum.name: httptimeout
enum.para: For HTTP(S) URIs, number of seconds to wait for a server response

enum.name: maxredirs
enum.para: Maximum number of redirects to follow. The default is -1, which allows for unlimited redirects. This only makes sense when followlocation is also set.

enum.name: proxy
enum.para: Hostname or IP address to use as a proxy server

enum.name: proxytype
enum.para: Type of proxy

enum.name: proxyport
enum.para: Port number of the proxy

enum.name: proxyuserpwd
enum.para: A username:password combination to use for authenticating requests through a proxy

enum.name: referer
enum.para: Referer URL to use for the request

enum.name: useragent
enum.para: UserAgent string to use for the request

enum.name: userpwd
enum.para: A username:password to use for authentication when the server response to an initial request indicates a 401 status code.

enum.name: ssl_verifypeer
enum.para: Whether to verify the server certificate against a list of known root certificate authorities (boolean).

enum.name: ssl_verifyhost
enum.para: Whether to verify the host in the server's TLS certificate. Set to 2 to verify the host, 0 to ignore the host.

enum.name: ssl_cainfo
enum.para: Path to a file holding one or more certificates to verify the peer's certificate with. Only used when ssl_verifypeer is enabled.

enum.name: ssl_capath
enum.para: Path to a directory holding multiple CA certificates to verify the peer's certificate with. Only used when ssl_verifypeer is enabled.

enum.name: ssl_cert
enum.para: Path to a file containing a client certificate. Default format is PEM, and can be changed with ssl_certtype.

enum.name: ssl_certtype
enum.para: The format of the ssl_cert file.

enum.name: ssl_key
enum.para: Path to a file containing a client private key. Default format is PEM, and can be changed with ssl_keytype

enum.name: ssl_keytype
enum.para: The format of the ssl_key file.

enum.name: ssl_keypasswd
enum.para: The passphrase to use the ssl_key file.

enum.name: hashcompat
enum.para: Assuming the responses will be in key1=value1&key2=value2 format, reformat the response such that it can be used by the HASH function.

enum.name: legacy
enum.para: Also translate + to the space character, in violation of current RFC standards.

enum.name: failurecodes
enum.para: A comma separated list of HTTP response codes to be treated as errors

description.para: Options may be set globally or per channel. Per-channel settings will override global settings. Only HTTP headers are added instead of overriding

function.name: SORT
function.synopsis: Sorts a list of key/vals into a list of keys, based upon the vals.

description.para: Takes a comma-separated list of keys and values, each separated by a colon, and returns a comma-separated list of the keys, sorted by their values. Values will be evaluated as floating-point numbers.

function.name: CUT
function.synopsis: Slices and dices strings, based upon a named delimiter.

parameter.name: varname
parameter.para: Variable you want cut

parameter.name: char-delim
parameter.para: Delimiter, defaults to -

parameter.name: range-spec
parameter.para: Number of the field you want (1-based offset), may also be specified as a range (with -) or group of ranges and fields (with &)

description.para: Cut out information from a string (varname), based upon a named delimiter.

example.title: The 'varname' parameter can only accept a variable name, not a variable expression

description.example: exten => s,1,Set(foo=${CUT(bar,,2)}); This is correct syntax exten => s,2,Set(foo=${CUT(${bar},,2)}); This is invalid syntax (unless bar contains the name of another variable)

function.name: DB
function.synopsis: Read from or write to the Asterisk database.

description.para: This function will read from or write a value to the Asterisk database. On a read, this function returns the corresponding value from the database, or blank if it does not exist. Reading a database value will also set the variable DB_RESULT. If you wish to find out if an entry exists, use the DB_EXISTS function.

function.name: DB_EXISTS
function.synopsis: Check to see if a key exists in the Asterisk database.

description.para: This function will check to see if a key exists in the Asterisk database. If it exists, the function will return 1. If not, it will return 0. Checking for existence of a database key will also set the variable DB_RESULT to the key's value if it exists.

function.name: DB_KEYS
function.synopsis: Obtain a list of keys within the Asterisk database.

description.para: This function will return a comma-separated list of keys existing at the prefix specified within the Asterisk database. If no argument is provided, then a list of key families will be returned.

function.name: DB_KEYCOUNT
function.synopsis: Obtain the number of keys at a prefix within the Asterisk database.

description.para: This function will return the number of keys that exist at the prefix specified within the Asterisk database. If no argument is provided, then the number of all key families will be returned.

function.name: DB_DELETE
function.synopsis: Return a value from the database and delete it.

description.para: This function will retrieve a value from the Asterisk database and then remove that key from the database. DB_RESULT will be set to the key's value if it exists.

note.para: If live_dangerously in asterisk.conf is set to no, this function can only be read from the dialplan, and not directly from external protocols. It can, however, be executed as a write operation (DB_DELETE(family, key)=ignored)

function.name: DEVICE_STATE
function.synopsis: Get or Set a device state.

description.para: The DEVICE_STATE function can be used to retrieve the device state from any device state provider. For example:
NoOp(SIP/mypeer has state ${DEVICE_STATE(SIP/mypeer)})
NoOp(Conference number 1234 has state ${DEVICE_STATE(MeetMe:1234)})
The DEVICE_STATE function can also be used to set custom device state from the dialplan. The Custom: prefix must be used. For example:
Set(DEVICE_STATE(Custom:lamp1)=BUSY)
Set(DEVICE_STATE(Custom:lamp2)=NOT_INUSE)
You can subscribe to the status of a custom device state using a hint in the dialplan:
exten => 1234,hint,Custom:lamp1
The possible values for both uses of this function are:
UNKNOWN | NOT_INUSE | INUSE | BUSY | INVALID | UNAVAILABLE | RINGING | RINGINUSE | ONHOLD

function.name: HINT
function.synopsis: Get the devices set for a dialplan hint.

option.name: n
option.para: Retrieve name on the hint instead of list of devices.

description.para: The HINT function can be used to retrieve the list of devices that are mapped to a dialplan hint.

function.name: DIALGROUP
function.synopsis: Manages a group of users for dialing.

parameter.name: op
parameter.para: The operation name, possible values are:
add - add a channel name or interface (write-only)
del - remove a channel name or interface (write-only)

description.para: Presents an interface meant to be used in concert with the Dial application, by presenting a list of channels which should be dialled when referenced.

When DIALGROUP is read from, the argument is interpreted as the particular group for which a dial should be attempted. When DIALGROUP is written to with no arguments, the entire list is replaced with the argument specified.

Functionality is similar to a queue, except that when no interfaces are available, execution may continue in the dialplan. This is useful when you want certain people to be the first to answer any calls, with immediate fallback to a queue when the front line people are busy or unavailable, but you still want front line people to log in and out of that group, just like a queue.

example.title: Add 2 endpoints to a dial group

function.name: DIALPLAN_EXISTS
function.synopsis: Checks the existence of a dialplan target.

description.para: This function returns 1 if the target exits. Otherwise, it returns 0.

function.name: VALID_EXTEN
function.synopsis: Determine whether an extension exists or not.

parameter.name: context
parameter.para: Defaults to the current context

parameter.name: priority
parameter.para: Priority defaults to 1.

description.para: Returns a true value if the indicated context, extension, and priority exist.

warning.para: This function has been deprecated in favor of the DIALPLAN_EXISTS() function

function.name: ENUMQUERY
function.synopsis: Initiate an ENUM query.

parameter.name: method-type
parameter.para: If no method-type is given, the default will be pjsip.

parameter.name: zone-suffix
parameter.para: If no zone-suffix is given, the default will be e164.arpa

description.para: This will do a ENUM lookup of the given phone number.

function.name: ENUMRESULT
function.synopsis: Retrieve results from a ENUMQUERY.

parameter.name: id
parameter.para: The identifier returned by the ENUMQUERY function.

parameter.name: resultnum
parameter.para: The number of the result that you want to retrieve.
Results start at 1. If this argument is specified as getnum, then it will return the total number of results that are available or -1 on error.

description.para: This function will retrieve results from a previous use of the ENUMQUERY function.

function.name: ENUMLOOKUP
function.synopsis: General or specific querying of NAPTR records for ENUM or ENUM-like DNS pointers.

parameter.name: method-type
parameter.para: If no method-type is given, the default will be pjsip.

option.name: c
option.para: Returns an integer count of the number of NAPTRs of a certain RR type.
Combination of c and Method-type of ALL will return a count of all NAPTRs for the record or -1 on error.

option.name: u
option.para: Returns the full URI and does not strip off the URI-scheme.

option.name: s
option.para: Triggers ISN specific rewriting.

option.name: i
option.para: Looks for branches into an Infrastructure ENUM tree.

option.name: d
option.para: for a direct DNS lookup without any flipping of digits.

parameter.name: record#
parameter.para: If no record# is given, defaults to 1.

parameter.name: zone-suffix
parameter.para: If no zone-suffix is given, the default will be e164.arpa

description.para: For more information see doc/AST.pdf.

function.name: TXTCIDNAME
function.synopsis: TXTCIDNAME looks up a caller name via DNS.

parameter.name: zone-suffix
parameter.para: If no zone-suffix is given, the default will be e164.arpa

description.para: This function looks up the given phone number in DNS to retrieve the caller id name. The result will either be blank or be the value found in the TXT record in DNS.

function.name: ENV

parameter.name: varname

Additionally, the following system variables are available as special built-in dialplan variables. These variables cannot be set or modified and are read-only.

function.name: STAT
function.synopsis: Does a check on the specified file.

parameter.name: flag
parameter.para: Flag may be one of the following:
d - Checks if the file is a directory.
e - Checks if the file exists.
f - Checks if the file is a regular file.
m - Returns the file mode (in octal)
s - Returns the size (in bytes) of the file
A - Returns the epoch at which the file was last accessed.
C - Returns the epoch at which the inode was last changed.
M - Returns the epoch at which the file was last modified.

note.para: If live_dangerously in asterisk.conf is set to no, this function can only be executed from the dialplan, and not directly from external protocols.

function.name: FILE
function.synopsis: Read or write text file.

parameter.name: offset
parameter.para: Maybe specified as any number. If negative, offset specifies the number of bytes back from the end of the file.

parameter.name: length
parameter.para: If specified, will limit the length of the data read to that size. If negative, trims length bytes from the end of the file.

option.name: l
option.para: Line mode: offset and length are assumed to be measured in lines, instead of byte offsets.

option.name: a
option.para: In write mode only, the append option is used to append to the end of the file, instead of overwriting the existing file.

option.name: d
option.para: In write mode and line mode only, this option does not automatically append a newline string to the end of a value. This is useful for deleting lines, instead of setting them to blank.

parameter.name: format
parameter.para: The format parameter may be used to delimit the type of line terminators in line mode.

option.name: u
option.para: Unix newline format.

option.name: d
option.para: DOS newline format.

option.name: m
option.para: Macintosh newline format.

description.para: Read and write text file in character and line mode.
Examples:
Read mode (byte):

example.title: Reads the entire content of the file
Reads from the 11th byte to the end of the file (i.e. skips the first 10)
Reads from the 11th to 20th byte in the file (i.e. skip the first 10, then read 10 bytes)

description.para: Read mode (line):

example.title: Reads the 3rd line of the file
Reads the 3rd and 4th lines of the file
Reads from the third line to the end of the file
Reads the last three lines of the file
Reads the 3rd line of a DOS-formatted file

description.para: Write mode (byte):

example.title: Truncate the file and write bar
Replace the first byte with bar (replaces 1 character with 3)
Replace 10 bytes beginning at the 21st byte of the file with bar
Replace all bytes from the 21st with bar

description.para: Write mode (line):

example.title: Replace the first line of the file with bar
Replace the last line of the file with bar
Append bar to the file with a newline

note.para: If live_dangerously in asterisk.conf is set to no, this function can only be executed from the dialplan, and not directly from external protocols.

function.name: FILE_COUNT_LINE
function.synopsis: Obtains the number of lines of a text file.

parameter.name: format
parameter.para: Format may be one of the following:

option.name: u
option.para: Unix newline format.

option.name: d
option.para: DOS newline format.

option.name: m
option.para: Macintosh newline format.

note.para: If not specified, an attempt will be made to determine the newline format type.

description.para: Returns the number of lines, or -1 on error.

note.para: If live_dangerously in asterisk.conf is set to no, this function can only be executed from the dialplan, and not directly from external protocols.

function.name: FILE_FORMAT
function.synopsis: Return the newline format of a text file.

description.para: Return the line terminator type:
'u' - Unix "\n" format
'd' - DOS "\r\n" format
'm' - Macintosh "\r" format
'x' - Cannot be determined

note.para: If live_dangerously in asterisk.conf is set to no, this function can only be executed from the dialplan, and not directly from external protocols.

function.name: BASENAME
function.synopsis: Return the name of a file.

description.para: Return the base file name, given a full file path.

function.name: DIRNAME
function.synopsis: Return the directory of a file.

description.para: Return the directory of a file, given a full file path.

function.name: EVAL_EXTEN
function.synopsis: Evaluates the contents of a dialplan extension and returns it as a string.

description.para: The EVAL_EXTEN function looks up a dialplan entry by context,extension,priority, evaluates the contents of a Return statement to resolve any variable or function references, and returns the result as a string.
You can use this function to create simple user-defined lookup tables or user-defined functions.

Any variables in the evaluated data will be resolved in the context of that extension. For example, ${EXTEN} would refer to the EVAL_EXTEN extension, not the extension in the context invoking the function. This behavior is similar to other applications, e.g. Gosub.
Extensions on which EVAL_EXTEN is invoked are not different from other extensions. However, the application at that extension is not executed. Only the application data is parsed and evaluated.
A limitation of this function is that the application at the specified extension isn't actually executed, and thus unlike a Gosub, you can't pass arguments in the EVAL_EXTEN function.
If you need the ability to evaluate more complex logic that cannot be done purely using functions, see EVAL_SUB.

function.name: EVAL_SUB
function.synopsis: Executes a Gosub and provides its return value as a string

description.para: The EVAL_SUB function executes up a dialplan location by context,extension,priority, with optional arguments and returns the contents of the Return statement. The arguments to EVAL_SUB are exactly like they are with Gosub.

This function is complementary to EVAL_EXTEN. However, it is more powerful, since it allows executing arbitrary dialplan and capturing some outcome as a dialplan function's return value, allowing it to be used in a variety of scenarios that do not allow executing dialplan directly but allow variables and functions to be used, and where using EVAL_EXTEN would be difficult or impossible.
Consequently, this function also allows you to implement your own arbitrary functions in dialplan, which can then be wrapped using the Asterisk function interface using EVAL_SUB.

While this function is primarily intended to be used for executing Gosub routines that are quick and do not interact with the channel, it is safe to execute arbitrary, even blocking, dialplan in the called subroutine. That said, this kind of usage is not recommended.
This function will always return, even if the channel is hung up.

example.title: Record whether a PSTN call is local

description.example:
[islocal] exten => _X!,1,ExecIf($[${LEN(${EXTEN})}<10]?Return(1)) same => n,Set(LOCAL(npanxx)=${EXTEN:-10:6}) same => n,ReturnIf(${EXISTS(${DB(localcall/${npanxx})})}?${DB(localcall/${npanxx})}) same => n,Set(LOCAL(islocal)=${SHELL(curl "https://example.com/islocal?npanxx=${EXTEN:-10:6}")}) same => n,Set(LOCAL(islocal)=${FILTER(A-Z,${islocal})}) same => n,Set(DB(localcall/${npanxx})=${islocal}) same => n,Return(${islocal})
[outgoing] exten => _1NXXNXXXXXX,1,Set(CDR(toll)=${IF($["${EVAL_SUB(islocal,${EXTEN},1)}"="Y"]?0:1)}) same => n,Dial(DAHDI/1/${EXTEN}) same => n,Hangup()
description.para: This example illustrates an example of logic that would be difficult to capture in a way that a single call to EVAL_EXTEN would return the same result. For one, conditionals are involved, and due to the way Asterisk parses dialplan, all functions in an application call are evaluated all the time, which may be undesirable if they cause side effects (e.g. making a cURL request) that should only happen in certain circumstances.

function.name: EXPORT
function.synopsis: Set variables or dialplan functions on any arbitrary channel that exists.

parameter.name: channel
parameter.para: The complete channel name: SIP/12-abcd1234.

parameter.name: var
parameter.para: Variable name

description.para: Allows setting variables or functions on any existing channel if it exists.

function.name: EXTENSION_STATE
function.synopsis: Get an extension's state.

parameter.name: context
parameter.para: If it is not specified defaults to default.

description.para: The EXTENSION_STATE function can be used to retrieve the state from any hinted extension. For example:
NoOp(1234@default has state ${EXTENSION_STATE(1234)})
NoOp(4567@home has state ${EXTENSION_STATE(4567@home)})
The possible values returned by this function are:

parameter.name: varname
parameter.para: Variable name

parameter.name: channel
parameter.para: If not specified will default to current channel. It is the complete channel name: SIP/12-abcd1234 or the prefix only SIP/12.

description.para: Implements a shared variable area, in which you may share variables between channels.
The variables used in this space are separate from the general namespace of the channel and thus SHARED(foo) and foo represent two completely different variables, despite sharing the same name.

Finally, realize that there is an inherent race between channels operating at the same time, fiddling with each others' internal variables, which is why this special variable namespace exists; it is to remind you that variables in the SHARED namespace may change at any time, without warning. You should therefore take special care to ensure that when using the SHARED namespace, you retrieve the variable and store it in a regular channel variable before using it in a set of calculations (or you might be surprised by the result).

function.name: JITTERBUFFER
function.synopsis: Add a Jitterbuffer to the Read side of the channel. This dejitters the audio stream before it reaches the Asterisk core. This is a write only function.

option.name: fixed
option.para: Set a fixed jitterbuffer on the channel.

option.name: adaptive
option.para: Set an adaptive jitterbuffer on the channel.

option.name: disabled
option.para: Remove a previously set jitterbuffer from the channel.

description.para: Jitterbuffers are constructed in two different ways. The first always take four arguments: max_size, resync_threshold, target_extra, and sync_video. Alternatively, a single argument of default can be provided, which will construct the default jitterbuffer for the given jitterbuffer type.
The arguments are:
max_size: Length in milliseconds of the buffer. Defaults to 200 ms.
resync_threshold: The length in milliseconds over which a timestamp difference will result in resyncing the jitterbuffer. Defaults to 1000ms.
target_extra: This option only affects the adaptive jitterbuffer. It represents the amount time in milliseconds by which the new jitter buffer will pad its size. Defaults to 40ms.
sync_video: This option enables video synchronization with the audio stream. It can be turned on and off. Defaults to off.

example.title: Fixed with 200ms max size and video sync support
Fixed with 200ms max size, resync threshold 1500
Adaptive with 200ms max size, 60ms target extra
Adaptive with 200ms max size and video sync support
Set a fixed jitterbuffer with defaults; then remove it

note.para: If a channel specifies a jitterbuffer due to channel driver configuration and the JITTERBUFFER function has set a jitterbuffer for that channel, the jitterbuffer set by the JITTERBUFFER function will take priority and the jitterbuffer set by the channel configuration will not be applied.

This value should not appear in the key or hierarchy of keys itself, except to delimit the hierarchy of keys.

This option has no effect on any other type of value.

description.para: The JSON_DECODE function retrieves the value of the given variable name and parses it as JSON, returning the value at a specified key. If the key cannot be found, an empty string is returned.

function.name: LOCK
function.synopsis: Attempt to obtain a named mutex.

description.para: Attempts to grab a named lock exclusively, and prevents other channels from obtaining the same lock. LOCK will wait for the lock to become available. Returns 1 if the lock was obtained or 0 on error.

note.para: To avoid the possibility of a deadlock, LOCK will only attempt to obtain the lock for 3 seconds if the channel already has another lock.
If live_dangerously in asterisk.conf is set to no, this function can only be executed from the dialplan, and not directly from external protocols.

function.name: TRYLOCK
function.synopsis: Attempt to obtain a named mutex.

description.para: Attempts to grab a named lock exclusively, and prevents other channels from obtaining the same lock. Returns 1 if the lock was available or 0 otherwise.

note.para: If live_dangerously in asterisk.conf is set to no, this function can only be executed from the dialplan, and not directly from external protocols.

function.name: UNLOCK
function.synopsis: Unlocks a named mutex.

description.para: Unlocks a previously locked mutex. Returns 1 if the channel had a lock or 0 otherwise.

note.para: It is generally unnecessary to unlock in a hangup routine, as any locks held are automatically freed when the channel is destroyed.
If live_dangerously in asterisk.conf is set to no, this function can only be executed from the dialplan, and not directly from external protocols.

The hook dialplan will have two variables available. HOOK_CHANNEL is the channel the hook is enabled on. HOOK_ID is the hook ID for enabling or disabling the hook.
