configObject.name: globals
configObject.synopsis: Options that apply to every parking lot

configOption.name: parkeddynamic
configOption.synopsis: Enables dynamically created parkinglots.

description.para: If the option is enabled then the following variables can be used to dynamically create new parking lots.

The PARKINGDYNAMIC variable specifies the parking lot to use as a template to create a dynamic parking lot. It is an error to specify a non-existent parking lot for the template. If not set then the default parking lot is used as the template.

The PARKINGDYNCONTEXT variable specifies the dialplan context to use for the newly created dynamic parking lot. If not set then the context from the parking lot template is used. The context is created if it does not already exist and the new parking lot needs to create extensions.

The PARKINGDYNEXTEN variable specifies the parkext to use for the newly created dynamic parking lot. If not set then the parkext is used from the parking lot template. If the template does not specify a parkext then no extensions are created for the newly created parking lot. The dynamic parking lot cannot be created if it needs to create extensions that overlap existing parking lot extensions. The only exception to this is for the parkext extension and only if neither of the overlaping parking lot's parkext is exclusive.
The PARKINGDYNPOS variable specifies the parking positions to use for the newly created dynamic parking lot. If not set then the parkpos from the parking lot template is used.

configObject.name: parking_lot
configObject.synopsis: Defined parking lots for res_parking to use to park calls on

configOption.name: context
configOption.synopsis: The name of the context where calls are parked and picked up from.

description.para: This option is only used if parkext is set.

configOption.name: parkext
configOption.synopsis: Extension to park calls to this parking lot.

description.para: If this option is used, this extension will automatically be created to place calls into parking lots. In addition, if parkext_exclusive is set for this parking lot, the name of the parking lot will be included in the application's arguments so that it only parks to this parking lot. The extension will be created in context. Using this option also creates extensions for retrieving parked calls from the parking spaces in the same context.

note.para: Generated parking extensions cannot overlap. The only exception is if neither overlapping parkext is exclusive.

configOption.name: parkext_exclusive
configOption.synopsis: If yes, the extension registered as parkext will park exclusively to this parking lot.

configOption.name: parkpos
configOption.synopsis: Numerical range of parking spaces which can be used to retrieve parked calls.

description.para: If parkext is set, these extensions will automatically be mapped in context in order to pick up calls parked to these parking spaces.

configOption.name: parkinghints
configOption.synopsis: If yes, this parking lot will add hints automatically for parking spaces.

configOption.name: parkingtime
configOption.synopsis: Amount of time a call will remain parked before giving up (in seconds).

configOption.name: parkedmusicclass
configOption.synopsis: Which music class to use for parked calls. They will use the default if unspecified.

configOption.name: comebacktoorigin
configOption.synopsis: Determines what should be done with the parked channel if no one picks it up before it times out.

description.para: Valid Options:

enum.name: yes
enum.para: Automatically have the parked channel dial the device that parked the call with dial timeout set by the parkingtime option. When the call times out an extension to dial the PARKER will automatically be created in the park-dial context with an extension of the flattened parker device name. If the call is not answered, the parked channel that is timing out will continue in the dial plan at that point if there are more priorities in the extension (which won't be the case unless the dialplan deliberately includes such priorities in the park-dial context through pattern matching or deliberately written flattened peer extensions).

enum.name: no
enum.para: Place the call into the PBX at comebackcontext instead. The extension will still be set as the flattened peer name. If an extension the flattened peer name isn't available then it will fall back to the s extension. If that also is unavailable it will attempt to fall back to s@default. The normal dial extension will still be created in the park-dial context with the extension also being the flattened peer name.

note.para: Flattened Peer Names - Extensions can not include slash characters since those are used for pattern matching. When a peer name is flattened, slashes become underscores. For example if the parker of a call is called SIP/0004F2040001 then flattened peer name and therefor the extensions created and used on timeouts will be SIP_0004F204001.
When parking times out and the channel returns to the dial plan, the following variables are set:

variable.name: PARKING_SPACE
variable.para: extension that the call was parked in prior to timing out.

variable.name: PARKEDLOT
variable.para: name of the lot that the call was parked in prior to timing out.

variable.name: PARKER
variable.para: The device that parked the call

variable.name: PARKER_FLAT
variable.para: The flat version of PARKER

configOption.name: comebackdialtime
configOption.synopsis: Timeout for the Dial extension created to call back the parker when a parked call times out.

configOption.name: comebackcontext
configOption.synopsis: Context where parked calls will enter the PBX on timeout when comebacktoorigin=no

description.para: The extension the call enters will prioritize the flattened peer name in this context. If the flattened peer name extension is unavailable, then the 's' extension in this context will be used. If that also is unavailable, the 's' extension in the 'default' context will be used.

configOption.name: courtesytone
configOption.synopsis: If the name of a sound file is provided, use this as the courtesy tone

description.para: By default, this tone is only played to the caller of a parked call. Who receives the tone can be changed using the parkedplay option.

enum.name: no

enum.name: caller
enum.para: Apply only to the call connecting with the call coming out of the parking lot.

enum.name: callee
enum.para: Apply only to the call coming out of the parking lot.

enum.name: both
enum.para: Apply to both sides.

note.para: If courtesy tone is not specified then this option will be ignored.

configOption.synopsis: Who to apply the DTMF parking feature to when parked calls are picked up or timeout.

description.para: The ACL module used by res_pjsip. This module is independent of endpoints and operates on all inbound SIP communication using res_pjsip.

There are two main ways of defining your ACL with the options provided. You can use the permit and deny options which act on IP addresses, or the contactpermit and contactdeny options which act on Contact header addresses in incoming REGISTER requests. You can combine the various options to create a mixed ACL.
Additionally, instead of defining an ACL with options, you can reference IP or Contact header ACLs from the file acl.conf by using the acl or contactacl options.

configInfo.name: res_pjsip_config_wizard
configInfo.synopsis: Module that provides simple configuration wizard capabilities.

description.para: This module allows creation of common PJSIP configuration scenarios without having to specify individual endpoint, aor, auth, identify and registration objects.

For example, the following configuration snippet would create the endpoint, aor, contact, auth and phoneprov objects necessary for a phone to get phone provisioning information, register, and make and receive calls. A hint is also created in the default context for extension 1000.
description.example: [myphone] type = wizard sends_auth = no accepts_auth = yes sends_registrations = no accepts_registrations = yes has_phoneprov = yes transport = ipv4 has_hint = yes hint_exten = 1000 inbound_auth/username = testname inbound_auth/password = test password endpoint/allow = ulaw endpoint/context = default phoneprov/MAC = 001122aa4455 phoneprov/PROFILE = profile1
description.para: The first 8 items are specific to the wizard. The rest of the items are passed verbatim to the underlying objects.
The following configuration snippet would create the endpoint, aor, contact, auth, identify and registration objects necessary for a trunk to another pbx or ITSP that requires registration.
description.example: [mytrunk] type = wizard sends_auth = yes accepts_auth = no sends_registrations = yes accepts_registrations = no transport = ipv4 remote_hosts = sip1.myitsp.com:5060,sip2.myitsp.com:5060 outbound_auth/username = testname outbound_auth/password = test password endpoint/allow = ulaw endpoint/context = default
description.para: Of course, any of the items in either example could be placed into templates and shared among wizard objects.
For more information, visit:
For more information, visit:

description.para: Will create the following entry in hint_context:
Normal dialplan precedence rules apply so if there's already a hint for this extension in hint_context, this one will be ignored. For more information, visit:

Any extensions.conf style variables specified are passed directly to the dialplan.
Normal dialplan precedence rules apply so if there's already a priority 1 application for this specific extension in hint_context, this one will be ignored. For more information, visit:

configOption.synopsis: Variables to be passed directly to the endpoint.

configOption.name: phoneprov/*
configOption.synopsis: Variables to be passed directly to the phoneprov object.

description.para: To activate phoneprov, at least phoneprov/MAC must be set.
This module provides alternatives to matching inbound requests to a configured endpoint. At least one of the matching mechanisms must be provided, or the object configuration is invalid.
The matching mechanisms are provided by the following configuration options:

enum.name: match
enum.para: Match by source IP address.

enum.name: match_header
enum.para: Match by SIP header.

note.para: If multiple matching criteria are provided then an inbound request will be matched to the endpoint if it matches any of the criteria.

configOption.name: endpoint
configOption.synopsis: Name of endpoint identified

configOption.name: match
configOption.synopsis: IP addresses or networks to match against.

description.para: The value is a comma-delimited list of IP addresses or hostnames.

IP addresses may have a subnet mask appended. The subnet mask may be written in either CIDR or dotted-decimal notation. Separate the IP address and subnet mask with a slash ('/'). A source port can also be specified by adding a colon (':') after the address but before the subnet mask, e.g. 3.2.1.0:5061/24. To specify a source port for an IPv6 address, the address itself must be enclosed in square brackets ('[2001:db8:0::1]:5060')

When a hostname is used, the behavior depends on whether srv_lookups is enabled and/or a source port is provided. If srv_lookups is enabled and a source port is not provided, Asterisk will perform an SRV lookup on the provided hostname, adding all of the A and AAAA records that are resolved.
If the SRV lookup fails, srv_lookups is disabled, or a source port is specified when the hostname is configured, Asterisk will resolve the hostname and add all A and AAAA records that are resolved.

configOption.name: srv_lookups
configOption.synopsis: Perform SRV lookups for provided hostnames.

description.para: When enabled, srv_lookups will perform SRV lookups for _sip._udp, _sip._tcp, and _sips._tcp of the given hostnames to determine additional addresses that traffic may originate from.

configOption.name: match_header
configOption.synopsis: Header/value pair to match against.

description.para: A SIP header whose value is used to match against. SIP requests containing the header, along with the specified value, will be mapped to the specified endpoint. The header must be specified with a :, as in match_header = SIPHeader: value.
The specified SIP header value can be a regular expression if the value is of the form /regex/.

note.para: Use of a regex is expensive so be sure you need to use a regex to match your endpoint.

configOption.name: match_request_uri
configOption.synopsis: Request URI to match against.

description.para: The SIP request URI is used to match against.
The specified SIP request URI can be a regular expression if the value is of the form /regex/.

note.para: Use of a regex is expensive so be sure you need to use a regex to match your endpoint.

configOption.name: type
configOption.synopsis: Must be of type 'identify'.

function.name: PJSIP_HEADER
function.synopsis: Gets headers from an inbound PJSIP channel. Adds, updates or removes the specified SIP header from an outbound PJSIP channel.

enum.name: read
enum.para: Returns instance number of header name. A * may be appended to name to iterate over all headers beginning with name.

enum.name: add
enum.para: Adds a new header name to this session.

enum.name: update
enum.para: Updates instance number of header name to a new value. The header must already exist.

enum.name: remove
enum.para: Removes all instances of previously added headers whose names match name. A * may be appended to name to remove all headers beginning with name. name may be set to a single * to clear all previously added headers. In all cases, the number of headers actually removed is returned.

parameter.name: name
parameter.para: The name of the header.

parameter.name: number
parameter.para: If there's more than 1 header with the same name, this specifies which header to read or update. If not specified, defaults to 1 meaning the first matching header. Not valid for add or remove.

description.para: PJSIP_HEADER allows you to read specific SIP headers from the inbound PJSIP channel as well as write(add, update, remove) headers on the outbound channel. One exception is that you can read headers that you have already added on the outbound channel.
Examples:

example.title: Set somevar to the value of the From header
Set via2 to the value of the 2nd Via header
Set xhdr to the value of the 1st X-header
Add an X-Myheader header with the value of myvalue
Add an X-Myheader header with an empty value
Update the value of the header named X-Myheader to newvalue

description.example: ; 'X-Myheader' must already exist or the call will fail. exten => 1,1,Set(PJSIP_HEADER(update,X-MyHeader)=newvalue)

example.title: Remove all headers whose names exactly match X-MyHeader
Remove all headers that begin with X-My

note.para: The remove action can be called by reading or writing PJSIP_HEADER.

example.title: Display the number of headers removed
Set a variable to the number of headers removed
Just remove them ignoring any count

note.para: If you call PJSIP_HEADER in a normal dialplan context you'll be operating on the caller's (incoming) channel which may not be what you want. To operate on the callee's (outgoing) channel call PJSIP_HEADER in a pre-dial handler.

function.name: PJSIP_INHERITABLE_HEADER
function.synopsis: Adds, updates or removes the specified SIP header from a PJSIP or non-PJSIP channel to be inherited to an outbound PJSIP channel.

enum.name: add
enum.para: Adds a new header name to this channel.

enum.name: update
enum.para: Updates instance number of header name to a new value. The header must already exist.

enum.name: remove
enum.para: Removes all instances of previously added headers whose names match name. A * may be appended to name to remove all headers beginning with name. name may be set to a single * to clear all previously added headers. In all cases, the number of headers actually removed is returned.

parameter.name: name
parameter.para: The name of the header.

parameter.name: number
parameter.para: If there's more than 1 header with the same name, this specifies which header to read or update. If not specified, defaults to 1 meaning the first matching header. Not valid for add or remove.

description.para: PJSIP_INHERITABLE_HEADER allows you to write specific SIP headers on a calling channel to be inherited by an outbound PJSIP channel.
Examples:

example.title: Add an inheritable X-Myheader header with the value of myvalue
Add an inheritable X-Myheader header with an empty value
Add an inheritable X-MyHeader that will be inherited by child channel
Update the value of the inheritable header named X-Myheader to newvalue

description.example: ; 'X-Myheader' must already exist or the call will fail. exten => 1,1,Set(PJSIP_INHERITABLE_HEADER(update,X-MyHeader)=newvalue)

example.title: Remove all inheritable headers whose names exactly match X-MyHeader
Remove all inheritable headers that begin with X-My

note.para: If you call PJSIP_INHERITABLE_HEADER in a normal dialplan context you'll be operating on the caller's channel which will then be inherited to the callee's (outgoing) channel. Inherited headers can be updated or removed via PJSIP_INHERITABLE_HEADER in a pre-dial handler.

Headers added via PJSIP_INHERITABLE_HEADER are separate from headers added via PJSIP_HEADER. A header added via PJSIP_INHERITABLE_HEADER can only be or removed modified by PJSIP_INHERITABLE_HEADER. A header added via PJSIP_HEADER can only be modified or removed by PJSIP_HEADER.

example.title: Set and modify headers on callee channel

description.example:
[handler] exten => modheader,1,Set(PJSIP_INHERITABLE_HEADER(update,X-MyHeader)=myvalue) same => n,Set(PJSIP_INHERITABLE_HEADER(update,X-MyHeader2)=myvalueX) same => n,Set(PJSIP_INHERITABLE_HEADER(remove,X-MyHeader2)=)
[somecontext] exten => 1,1,Set(PJSIP_INHERITABLE_HEADER(add,X-MyHeader1)=myvalue1) same => n,Set(PJSIP_INHERITABLE_HEADER(add,X-MyHeader2)=myvalue2) same => n,Set(PJSIP_INHERITABLE_HEADER(add,X-MyHeader3)=myvalue3) same => n,Dial(PJSIP/${EXTEN},,b(handler^modheader^1))

function.name: PJSIP_HEADERS
function.synopsis: Gets the list of SIP header names from an INVITE message.

parameter.name: prefix
parameter.para: If specified, only the headers matching the given prefix are returned.

description.para: Returns a comma-separated list of header names (without values) from the INVITE message. Multiple headers with the same name are included in the list only once.
For example, ${PJSIP_HEADERS(Co)} might return Contact,Content-Length,Content-Type. As a practical example, you may use ${PJSIP_HEADERS(X-)} to enumerate optional extended headers.

function.name: PJSIP_RESPONSE_HEADER
function.synopsis: Gets headers of 200 response from an outbound PJSIP channel.

enum.name: read
enum.para: Returns instance number of response header name.

parameter.name: name
parameter.para: The name of the response header. A * can be appended to the name to iterate over all response headers beginning with name.

parameter.name: number
parameter.para: If there's more than 1 header with the same name, this specifies which header to read. If not specified, defaults to 1 meaning the first matching header.

description.para: PJSIP_RESPONSE_HEADER allows you to read specific SIP headers of 200 response from the outbound PJSIP channel.
Examples:

example.title: Set 'somevar' to the value of the 'From' header
Set 'via2' to the value of the 2nd 'Via' header
Set 'xhdr' to the value of the 1sx X-header

note.para: If you call PJSIP_RESPONSE_HEADER in a normal dialplan context you'll be operating on the caller's (incoming) channel which may not be what you want. To operate on the callee's (outgoing) channel call PJSIP_RESPONSE_HEADER in a pre-connect handler.

function.name: PJSIP_RESPONSE_HEADERS
function.synopsis: Gets the list of SIP header names from the 200 response of INVITE message.

parameter.name: prefix
parameter.para: If specified, only the headers matching the given prefix are returned.

description.para: Returns a comma-separated list of header names (without values) from the 200 response of INVITE message. Multiple headers with the same name are included in the list only once.
For example, ${PJSIP_RESPONSE_HEADERS(Co)} might return Contact,Content-Length,Content-Type. As a practical example, you may use ${PJSIP_RESPONSE_HEADERS(X-)} to enumerate optional extended headers.

function.name: PJSIP_HEADER_PARAM
function.synopsis: Get or set header/URI parameters on a PJSIP channel.

parameter.name: header_name
parameter.para: Header in which parameter should be read or set.
Currently, the only supported header is From.

parameter.name: parameter_type
parameter.para: The type of parameter to get or set.
Default is header parameter.

enum.name: header
enum.para: Header parameter.

enum.name: uri
enum.para: URI parameter.

parameter.name: parameter_name
parameter.para: Name of parameter.

description.para: PJSIP_HEADER_PARAM allows you to read or set parameters in a SIP header on a PJSIP channel.
Both URI parameters and header parameters can be read and set using this function. URI parameters appear in the URI (inside the <> in the header) while header parameters appear afterwards.

note.para: If you call PJSIP_HEADER_PARAM in a normal dialplan context you'll be operating on the caller's (incoming) channel which may not be what you want. To operate on the callee's (outgoing) channel call PJSIP_HEADER_PARAM in a pre-dial handler.

example.title: Set URI parameter in From header on outbound channel
Read URI parameter in From header on inbound channel

manager.name: PJSIPSetMaintenance
manager.synopsis: Enable or disable maintenance mode for a PJSIP endpoint.

parameter.name: Endpoint
parameter.para: The PJSIP endpoint name, or all to toggle maintenance mode for every configured endpoint.

parameter.name: State
parameter.para: Desired maintenance state.

description.para: Enables or disables maintenance mode for the specified PJSIP endpoint. While in maintenance mode, new inbound out-of-dialog requests are rejected with 503 Service Unavailable (except SUBSCRIBE/REGISTER with Expires: 0), and outbound originations via Dial() or ARI are refused before any SIP session or channel is created. In-progress dialogs are unaffected.
A PJSIPMaintenanceStatus event is emitted when the state changes.

manager.name: PJSIPShowMaintenance
manager.synopsis: Show maintenance mode status for PJSIP endpoints.

parameter.name: Endpoint
parameter.para: If specified, show the status for this endpoint only. If omitted, list all endpoints currently in maintenance mode.

description.para: Emits one PJSIPMaintenanceStatus event per result, followed by a PJSIPMaintenanceStatusComplete event.

managerEventInstance.synopsis: Reports the maintenance mode state of a PJSIP endpoint.

parameter.name: Endpoint
parameter.para: The PJSIP endpoint name.

parameter.name: Status
parameter.para: Current maintenance state.

description.para: Emitted when an endpoint enters or leaves maintenance mode, and as a list entry in response to PJSIPShowMaintenance.

info.name: MessageDestinationInfo
info.para: The destination parameter is used to construct the Request URI for an outgoing message. It can be in one of the following formats, all prefixed with the pjsip: message tech.

enum.name: endpoint
enum.para: Request URI comes from the endpoint's default aor and contact.

enum.name: endpoint/aor
enum.para: Request URI comes from the specific aor/contact.

enum.name: endpoint@domain
enum.para: Request URI from the endpoint's default aor and contact. The domain is discarded.

info.para: These all use the endpoint to send the message with the specified URI:
These all use the default endpoint to send the message with the specified URI:
These use the default endpoint to send the message with the specified host:
This form is similar to a dialstring:

You still need to prefix the destination with the pjsip: message technology prefix. For example: pjsip:PJSIP/8005551212@myprovider. The endpoint contact's URI will have the user inserted into it and will become the Request URI. If the contact URI already has a user specified, it will be replaced.

info.name: MessageFromInfo
info.para: The from parameter is used to specity the From: header in the outgoing SIP MESSAGE. It will override the value specified in MESSAGE(from) which itself will override any from value from an incoming SIP MESSAGE.

info.name: MessageToInfo
info.para: The to parameter is used to specity the To: header in the outgoing SIP MESSAGE. It will override the value specified in MESSAGE(to) which itself will override any to value from an incoming SIP MESSAGE.

manager.name: PJSIPNotify
manager.synopsis: Send a NOTIFY to either an endpoint, an arbitrary URI, or inside a SIP dialog.

parameter.name: Endpoint
parameter.para: The endpoint to which to send the NOTIFY.

parameter.name: URI
parameter.para: Abritrary URI to which to send the NOTIFY.

parameter.name: channel
parameter.para: Channel name to send the NOTIFY. Must be a PJSIP channel.

parameter.name: Option
parameter.para: The config section name from pjsip_notify.conf to use.
One of Option or Variable must be specified.

parameter.name: Variable
parameter.para: Appends variables as headers/content to the NOTIFY. If the variable is named Content, then the value will compose the body of the message if another variable sets Content-Type. name=value
One of Option or Variable must be specified.

description.para: Sends a NOTIFY to an endpoint, an arbitrary URI, or inside a SIP dialog.
All parameters for this event must be specified in the body of this request via multiple Variable: name=value sequences.

note.para: One (and only one) of Endpoint, URI, or Channel must be specified. If URI is used, the default outbound endpoint will be used to send the message. If the default outbound endpoint isn't configured, this command can not send to an arbitrary URI.

configInfo.name: res_pjsip_notify
configInfo.synopsis: Module that supports sending NOTIFY requests to endpoints from external sources

description.para: Each key-value pair in a notify configuration section defines either a SIP header to send in the request or a line of content in the request message body. A key of Content is treated as part of the message body and is appended in sequential order; any other header is treated as part of the SIP request.

configOption.synopsis: A key/value pair to add to a NOTIFY request.

description.para: If the key is Content, it will be treated as part of the message body. Otherwise, it will be added as a header in the NOTIFY request.
The following headers are reserved and cannot be specified:
This module allows res_pjsip to publish to other SIP servers.
Publish is COMPLETELY separate from the rest of pjsip.conf. A minimal configuration consists of setting a server_uri and event.

configOption.name: expiration
configOption.synopsis: Expiration time for publications in seconds

configOption.name: outbound_auth
configOption.synopsis: Authentication object(s) to be used for outbound publishes.

description.para: This is a comma-delimited list of auth sections defined in pjsip.conf used to respond to outbound authentication challenges.

note.para: Using the same auth section for inbound and outbound authentication is not recommended. There is a difference in meaning for an empty realm setting between inbound and outbound authentication uses. See the auth realm description for details.

configOption.name: outbound_proxy
configOption.synopsis: Full SIP URI of the outbound proxy used to send publishes

description.para: Proxy through which to send requests, a full SIP URI must be provided (default: ""). Consider adding \;lr for loose routing (to keep user@domain in the request URI).

configOption.name: server_uri
configOption.synopsis: SIP URI of the server and entity to publish to

description.para: This is the URI at which to find the entity and server to send the outbound PUBLISH to. This URI is used as the request URI of the outbound PUBLISH request from Asterisk.

configOption.name: from_uri
configOption.synopsis: SIP URI to use in the From header

description.para: This is the URI that will be placed into the From header of outgoing PUBLISH messages. If no URI is specified then the URI provided in server_uri will be used.

configOption.name: to_uri
configOption.synopsis: SIP URI to use in the To header

description.para: This is the URI that will be placed into the To header of outgoing PUBLISH messages. If no URI is specified then the URI provided in server_uri will be used.

configOption.name: event
configOption.synopsis: Event type of the PUBLISH.

configOption.name: max_auth_attempts
configOption.synopsis: Maximum number of authentication attempts before stopping the publication.

configOption.name: transport
configOption.synopsis: Transport used for outbound publish

note.para: A transport configured in pjsip.conf. As with other res_pjsip modules, this will use the first available transport of the appropriate type if unconfigured.

configOption.name: multi_user
configOption.synopsis: Enable multi-user support

description.para: When enabled the user portion of the server uri is replaced by a dynamically created user

configOption.name: type
configOption.synopsis: Must be of type 'outbound-publish'.

description.para: This module allows res_pjsip to register to other SIP servers.
Registration is COMPLETELY separate from the rest of pjsip.conf. A minimal configuration consists of setting a server_uri and a client_uri.

configOption.name: auth_rejection_permanent
configOption.synopsis: Determines whether failed authentication challenges are treated as permanent failures.

description.para: If this option is enabled and an authentication challenge fails, registration will not be attempted again until the configuration is reloaded.

configOption.name: client_uri
configOption.synopsis: Client SIP URI used when attemping outbound registration

description.para: This is the address-of-record for the outbound registration (i.e. the URI in the To header of the REGISTER).

For registration with an ITSP, the client SIP URI may need to consist of an account name or number and the provider's hostname for their registrar, e.g. client_uri=1234567890@example.com. This may differ between providers.
For registration to generic registrars, the client SIP URI will depend on networking specifics and configuration of the registrar.

configOption.name: contact_user
configOption.synopsis: Contact User to use in request. If this value is not set, this defaults to 's'

configOption.name: contact_header_params
configOption.synopsis: Header parameters to place in the Contact header

configOption.name: expiration
configOption.synopsis: Expiration time for registrations in seconds

configOption.name: max_retries
configOption.synopsis: Maximum number of registration attempts.

description.para: This sets the maximum number of registration attempts that are made before stopping any further attempts. If set to 0 then upon failure no further attempts are made.

configOption.name: security_negotiation
configOption.synopsis: The kind of security agreement negotiation to use. Currently, only mediasec is supported.

configOption.name: security_mechanisms
configOption.synopsis: List of security mechanisms supported.

description.para: This is a comma-delimited list of security mechanisms to use. Each security mechanism must be in the form defined by RFC 3329 section 2.2.

configOption.name: outbound_auth
configOption.synopsis: Authentication object(s) to be used for outbound registrations.

description.para: This is a comma-delimited list of auth sections defined in pjsip.conf used to respond to outbound authentication challenges.

note.para: Using the same auth section for inbound and outbound authentication is not recommended. There is a difference in meaning for an empty realm setting between inbound and outbound authentication uses. See the auth realm description for details.

configOption.name: outbound_proxy
configOption.synopsis: Full SIP URI of the outbound proxy used to send registrations

configOption.name: max_random_initial_delay
configOption.synopsis: Maximum interval in seconds for which an initial registration may be randomly delayed

description.para: By default, registrations are randomly delayed by a small amount to prevent too many registrations from being made simultaneously.
Depending on your system usage, it may be desirable to set this to a smaller or larger value to have fine grained control over the size of this random delay.

configOption.name: retry_interval
configOption.synopsis: Interval in seconds between retries if outbound registration is unsuccessful

configOption.name: forbidden_retry_interval
configOption.synopsis: Interval used when receiving a 403 Forbidden response.

description.para: If a 403 Forbidden is received, chan_pjsip will wait forbidden_retry_interval seconds before attempting registration again. If 0 is specified, chan_pjsip will not retry after receiving a 403 Forbidden response. Setting this to a non-zero value goes against a "SHOULD NOT" in RFC3261, but can be used to work around buggy registrars.

configOption.name: fatal_retry_interval
configOption.synopsis: Interval used when receiving a Fatal response.

description.para: If a fatal response is received, chan_pjsip will wait fatal_retry_interval seconds before attempting registration again. If 0 is specified, chan_pjsip will not retry after receiving a fatal (non-temporary 4xx, 5xx, 6xx) response. Setting this to a non-zero value may go against a "SHOULD NOT" in RFC3261, but can be used to work around buggy registrars.

note.para: if also set the forbidden_retry_interval takes precedence over this one when a 403 is received. Also, if auth_rejection_permanent equals 'yes' then a 401 and 407 become subject to this retry interval.

configOption.name: server_uri
configOption.synopsis: SIP URI of the server to register against

description.para: This is the URI at which to find the registrar to send the outbound REGISTER. This URI is used as the request URI of the outbound REGISTER request from Asterisk.
For registration with an ITSP, the setting may often be just the domain of the registrar, e.g. sip:sip.example.com.

configOption.name: transport
configOption.synopsis: Transport used for outbound authentication

note.para: A transport configured in pjsip.conf. As with other res_pjsip modules, this will use the first available transport of the appropriate type if unconfigured.

configOption.name: line
configOption.synopsis: Whether to add a 'line' parameter to the Contact for inbound call matching

description.para: When enabled this option will cause a 'line' parameter to be added to the Contact header placed into the outgoing registration request. If the remote server sends a call this line parameter will be used to establish a relationship to the outbound registration, ultimately causing the configured endpoint to be used.

configOption.name: endpoint
configOption.synopsis: Endpoint to use for incoming related calls

description.para: When line support is enabled this configured endpoint name is used for incoming calls that are related to the outbound registration.

configOption.name: type
configOption.synopsis: Must be of type 'registration'.

configOption.name: support_path
configOption.synopsis: Enables advertising SIP Path support for outbound REGISTER requests.

description.para: When this option is enabled, outbound REGISTER requests will advertise support for Path headers so that intervening proxies can add to the Path header as necessary.

configOption.name: support_outbound
configOption.synopsis: Enables advertising SIP Outbound support (RFC5626) for outbound REGISTER requests.

configOption.name: user_agent
configOption.synopsis: Overrides the User-Agent header that should be used for outbound REGISTER requests.

parameter.name: Registration
parameter.para: The outbound registration to unregister or '*all' to unregister them all.

description.para: Unregisters the specified (or all) outbound registration(s) and stops future registration attempts. Call PJSIPRegister to start registration and schedule re-registrations according to configuration.

parameter.name: Registration
parameter.para: The outbound registration to register or '*all' to register them all.

description.para: Unregisters the specified (or all) outbound registration(s) then starts registration and schedules re-registrations according to configuration.

In response OutboundRegistrationDetail events showing configuration and status information are raised for each outbound registration object. AuthDetail events are raised for each associated auth object as well. Once all events are completed an OutboundRegistrationDetailComplete is issued.

managerEventInstance.synopsis: Provides configuration details and status information about an outbound registration.

parameter.name: ObjectType
parameter.para: The object's type. This will always be 'registration'.

parameter.name: ObjectName
parameter.para: The name of this object.

parameter.name: Status
parameter.para: The current status of this registration. Will be one of:

parameter.name: NextReg
parameter.para: The number of seconds until the next registration.

configInfo.name: res_pjsip_phoneprov_provider
configInfo.synopsis: Module that integrates res_pjsip with res_phoneprov.

description.para: This module creates the integration between res_pjsip and res_phoneprov.

Each user to be integrated requires a phoneprov section defined in pjsip.conf. Each section identifies the endpoint associated with the user and any other name/value pairs to be passed on to res_phoneprov's template substitution. Only MAC and PROFILE variables are required. Any other variables supplied will be passed through.
Example:
type = phoneprovr
endpoint = ep1000
MAC = deadbeef4dad
PROFILE = grandstream2
LINEKEYS = 2
LINE = 1
OTHERVAR = othervalue
The following variables are automatically defined if an endpoint is defined for the user:

enum.name: USERNAME
enum.para: Source: The user_name defined in the first auth reference in the endpoint.

enum.name: SECRET
enum.para: Source: The user_pass defined in the first auth reference in the endpoint.

enum.name: CALLERID
enum.para: Source: The number part of the callerid defined in the endpoint.

enum.name: DISPLAY_NAME
enum.para: Source: The name part of the callerid defined in the endpoint.

enum.name: LABEL
enum.para: Source: The id of the phoneprov section.

description.para: In addition to the standard variables, the following are also automatically defined:

enum.name: ENDPOINT_ID
enum.para: Source: The id of the endpoint.

enum.name: TRANSPORT_ID
enum.para: Source: The id of the transport used by the endpoint.

enum.name: AUTH_ID
enum.para: Source: The id of the auth used by the endpoint.

description.para: All other template substitution variables must be explicitly defined in the phoneprov_default or phoneprov sections.

configOption.name: type
configOption.synopsis: Must be of type 'phoneprov'.

configOption.name: endpoint
configOption.synopsis: The endpoint from which variables will be retrieved.

configOption.name: MAC
configOption.synopsis: The mac address for this user. (required)

configOption.name: PROFILE
configOption.synopsis: The phoneprov profile to use for this user. (required)
Other name/value pairs to be passed through for use in templates.

configInfo.name: res_pjsip_publish_asterisk
configInfo.synopsis: SIP resource for inbound and outbound Asterisk event publications

para.emphasis: Inbound and outbound Asterisk event publication

description.para: This module allows res_pjsip to send and receive Asterisk event publications.

configObject.name: asterisk-publication
configObject.synopsis: The configuration for inbound Asterisk event publication

description.para: Publish is COMPLETELY separate from the rest of pjsip.conf.

configOption.name: devicestate_publish
configOption.synopsis: Optional name of a publish item that can be used to publish a request for full device state information.

configOption.name: mailboxstate_publish
configOption.synopsis: Optional name of a publish item that can be used to publish a request for full mailbox state information.

configOption.name: device_state
configOption.synopsis: Whether we should permit incoming device state events.

configOption.name: device_state_filter
configOption.synopsis: Optional regular expression used to filter what devices we accept events for.

configOption.name: mailbox_state
configOption.synopsis: Whether we should permit incoming mailbox state events.

configOption.name: mailbox_state_filter
configOption.synopsis: Optional regular expression used to filter what mailboxes we accept events for.

configOption.name: type
configOption.synopsis: Must be of type 'asterisk-publication'.

description.para: Provides a listing of all inbound subscriptions. An event InboundSubscriptionDetail is issued for each subscription object. Once all detail events are completed an InboundSubscriptionDetailComplete event is issued.

managerEventInstance.synopsis: Provides details about an inbound subscription - one in which Asterisk handles SUBSCRIBE requests and periodically sends NOTIFYs to its subscribers.

parameter.name: Role
parameter.para: Asterisk's role for this subscription. This will always be Notifier.

parameter.name: Endpoint
parameter.para: The name of the endpoint associated with this subscription.

parameter.name: Callid
parameter.para: The CallID of the dialog associated with this subscription.

parameter.name: State
parameter.para: The current state of the subscription.

parameter.name: Callerid
parameter.para: The Caller ID of the endpoint associated with this subscription.

parameter.name: SubscriptionType
parameter.para: Asterisk currently supports the following subscription types, but this could also be extended by third-party modules so this list may not be exhaustive:

parameter.name: Extension
parameter.para: If the SubscriptionType is extension_state this will be the monitored extension.

parameter.name: ExtensionStates
parameter.para: If the SubscriptionType is extension_state this will be the monitored extension's state.

parameter.name: Mailboxes
parameter.para: If the SubscriptionType is mwi this will be a comma-separated list of mailboxes.

description.para: Provides a listing of all outbound subscriptions. An event OutboundSubscriptionDetail is issued for each subscription object. Once all detail events are completed an OutboundSubscriptionDetailComplete event is issued.

managerEventInstance.synopsis: Provides details about an outbound subscription - one in which Asterisk sends SUBSCRIBE requests and periodically receives NOTIFYs.

parameter.name: Role
parameter.para: Asterisk's role for this subscription. This will always be Subscriber.

parameter.name: Endpoint
parameter.para: The name of the endpoint associated with this subscription.

parameter.name: Callid
parameter.para: The CallID of the dialog associated with this subscription.

parameter.name: State
parameter.para: The current state of the subscription.

parameter.name: Callerid
parameter.para: The Caller ID of the endpoint associated with this subscription.

parameter.name: SubscriptionType
parameter.para: Asterisk currently supports the following subscription types, but this could also be extended by third-party modules so this list may not be exhaustive:

parameter.name: Extension
parameter.para: If the SubscriptionType is extension_state this will be the monitored extension.

parameter.name: ExtensionStates
parameter.para: If the SubscriptionType is extension_state this will be the monitored extension's state.

parameter.name: Mailboxes
parameter.para: If the SubscriptionType is mwi this will be a comma-separated list of mailboxes.

manager.name: PJSIPShowResourceLists
manager.synopsis: Displays settings for configured resource lists.

description.para: Provides a listing of all resource lists. An event ResourceListDetail is issued for each resource list object. Once all detail events are completed a ResourceListDetailComplete event is issued.

managerEventInstance.synopsis: Provides details about a resource list.

parameter.name: ObjectType

configObject.synopsis: Persists SIP subscriptions so they survive restarts.

configOption.synopsis: The local address the subscription was received on

configOption.name: local_port
configOption.synopsis: The local port the subscription was received on

configOption.name: cseq
configOption.synopsis: The sequence number of the next NOTIFY to be sent

configOption.name: tag
configOption.synopsis: The local tag of the dialog for the subscription

configOption.name: endpoint
configOption.synopsis: The name of the endpoint that subscribed

configOption.name: expires
configOption.synopsis: The time at which the subscription expires

configOption.name: contact_uri
configOption.synopsis: The Contact URI of the dialog for the subscription

configOption.name: prune_on_boot
configOption.synopsis: If set, indicates that the contact used a reliable transport and therefore the subscription must be deleted after an asterisk restart.

configOption.name: generator_data

description.para: This configuration object allows for RFC 4662 resource list subscriptions to be specified. This can be useful to decrease the amount of subscription traffic that a server has to process.

note.para: Current limitations limit the size of SIP NOTIFY requests that Asterisk sends to double that of the PJSIP maximum packet length. If your resource list notifications are larger than this maximum, you will need to make adjustments.

configOption.name: type
configOption.synopsis: Must be of type 'resource_list'

configOption.name: event
configOption.synopsis: The SIP event package that the list resource belong to.

description.para: The SIP event package describes the types of resources that Asterisk reports the state of.

enum.name: presence
enum.para: Device state and presence reporting.

enum.name: dialog
enum.para: This is identical to presence.

enum.name: message-summary
enum.para: Message-waiting indication (MWI) reporting.

configOption.name: list_item
configOption.synopsis: The name of a resource to report state on

description.para: In general Asterisk looks up list items in the following way:
1. Check if the list item refers to another configured resource list.
2. Pass the name of the resource off to event-package-specific handlers to find the specified resource.

The second part means that the way the list item is specified depends on what type of list this is. For instance, if you have the event set to presence, then list items should be in the form of dialplan_extension@dialplan_context. For message-summary mailbox names should be listed.

configOption.name: full_state
configOption.synopsis: Indicates if the entire list's state should be sent out.

description.para: If this option is enabled, and a resource changes state, then Asterisk will construct a notification that contains the state of all resources in the list. If the option is disabled, Asterisk will construct a notification that only contains the states of resources that have changed.

note.para: Even with this option disabled, there are certain situations where Asterisk is forced to send a notification with the states of all resources in the list. When a subscriber renews or terminates its subscription to the list, Asterisk MUST send a full state notification.

configOption.name: notification_batch_interval
configOption.synopsis: Time Asterisk should wait, in milliseconds, before sending notifications.

description.para: When a resource's state changes, it may be desired to wait a certain amount before Asterisk sends a notification to subscribers. This allows for other state changes to accumulate, so that Asterisk can communicate multiple state changes in a single notification instead of rapidly sending many notifications.

configOption.name: resource_display_name
configOption.synopsis: Indicates whether display name of resource or the resource name being reported.

description.para: If this option is enabled, the Display Name will be reported as resource name. If the event set to presence or dialog, the non-empty HINT name will be set as the Display Name. The message-summary is not supported yet.

configOption.name: endpoint
configOption.synopsis: Optional name of an endpoint that is only allowed to publish to this resource

configOption.name: type
configOption.synopsis: Must be of type 'inbound-publication'.

description.para: In response, InboundRegistrationDetail events showing configuration and status information are raised for all contacts, static or dynamic. Once all events are completed an InboundRegistrationDetailComplete is issued.

warning.para: This command just dumps all coonfigured AORs with contacts, even if the contact is a permanent one. To really get just inbound registrations, use PJSIPShowRegistrationInboundContactStatuses.

manager.name: PJSIPShowRegistrationInboundContactStatuses
manager.synopsis: Lists ContactStatuses for PJSIP inbound registrations.

description.para: In response, ContactStatusDetail events showing status information are raised for each inbound registration (dynamic contact) object. Once all events are completed a ContactStatusDetailComplete event is issued.

parameter.para: The object's type. This will always be 'aor'.

parameter.name: ObjectName

description.para: The general settings section contains information to configure Asterisk to serve up statistics for a Prometheus server.

note.para: You must enable Asterisk's HTTP server in http.conf for this module to function properly!

configOption.name: enabled
configOption.synopsis: Enable or disable Prometheus statistics.

configOption.name: core_metrics_enabled
configOption.synopsis: Enable or disable core metrics.

description.para: Core metrics show various properties of the Asterisk system, including how the binary was built, the version, uptime, last reload time, etc. Generally, these options are harmless and should always be enabled. This option mostly exists to disable output of all options for testing purposes, as well as for those foolish souls who really don't care what version of Asterisk they're running.

configOption.name: uri
configOption.synopsis: The HTTP URI to serve metrics up on.

configOption.name: auth_username
configOption.synopsis: Username to use for Basic Auth.

description.para: If set, use Basic Auth to authenticate requests to the route specified by uri. Note that you will need to configure your Prometheus server with the appropriate auth credentials.
If set, auth_password must also be set appropriately.

warning.para: It is highly recommended to set up Basic Auth. Failure to do so may result in useful information about your Asterisk system being made easily scrapable by the wide world. Consider yourself duly warned.

configOption.name: auth_password
configOption.synopsis: Password to use for Basic Auth.

description.para: If set, this is used in conjunction with auth_username to require Basic Auth for all requests to the Prometheus metrics. Note that setting this without auth_username will not do anything.

configOption.name: auth_realm
configOption.synopsis: Auth realm used in challenge responses

configOption.name: hosts
configOption.synopsis: Full path to an optional hosts file

description.para: Hosts specified in a hosts file will be resolved within the resolver itself. If a value of system is provided the system-specific file will be used.

configOption.name: resolv
configOption.synopsis: Full path to an optional resolv.conf file

description.para: The resolv.conf file specifies the nameservers to contact when resolving queries. If a value of system is provided the system-specific file will be used. If provided alongside explicit nameservers the nameservers contained within the resolv.conf file will be used after all others.

configOption.name: nameserver
configOption.synopsis: Nameserver to use for queries

description.para: An explicit nameserver can be specified which is used for resolving queries. If multiple nameserver lines are specified the first will be the primary with failover occurring, in order, to the other nameservers as backups. If provided alongside a resolv.conf file the nameservers explicitly specified will be used before all others.

configOption.name: debug
configOption.synopsis: Unbound debug level

description.para: The debugging level for the unbound resolver. While there is no explicit range generally the higher the number the more debug is output.

configOption.name: ta_file
configOption.synopsis: Trust anchor file

description.para: Full path to a file with DS and DNSKEY records in zone file format. This file is provided to unbound and is used as a source for trust anchors.

function.name: SMDI_MSG_RETRIEVE
function.synopsis: Retrieve an SMDI message.

enum.name: t
enum.para: Instead of searching on the forwarding station, search on the message desk terminal.

enum.name: n
enum.para: Instead of searching on the forwarding station, search on the message desk number.

description.para: This function is used to retrieve an incoming SMDI message. It returns an ID which can be used with the SMDI_MSG() function to access details of the message. Note that this is a destructive function in the sense that once an SMDI message is retrieved using this function, it is no longer in the global SMDI message queue, and can not be accessed by any other Asterisk channels. The timeout for this function is optional, and the default is 3 seconds. When providing a timeout, it should be in milliseconds.
The default search is done on the forwarding station ID. However, if you set one of the search key options in the options field, you can change this behavior.

function.name: SMDI_MSG
function.synopsis: Retrieve details about an SMDI message.

parameter.name: component
parameter.para: Valid message components are:

enum.name: number
enum.para: The message desk number

enum.name: terminal
enum.para: The message desk terminal

enum.name: station
enum.para: The forwarding station

enum.name: callerid
enum.para: The callerID of the calling party that was forwarded

enum.name: type
enum.para: The call type. The value here is the exact character that came in on the SMDI link. Typically, example values are:
Options:

enum.name: D
enum.para: Direct Calls

enum.name: A
enum.para: Forward All Calls

enum.name: B
enum.para: Forward Busy Calls

enum.name: N
enum.para: Forward No Answer Calls

description.para: This function is used to access details of an SMDI message that was pulled from the incoming SMDI message queue using the SMDI_MSG_RETRIEVE() function.

The res_statsd module provides an API that allows Asterisk and its modules to send statistics to a StatsD server. It only provides a means to communicate with a StatsD server and does not send any metrics of its own.
An example module, res_chan_stats, is provided which uses the API exposed by this module to send channel statistics to the configured StatsD server.
More information about StatsD can be found at https://github.com/statsd/statsd

configOption.name: enabled
configOption.synopsis: Enable/disable the StatsD module

configOption.name: server
configOption.synopsis: Address of the StatsD server

configOption.name: prefix
configOption.synopsis: Prefix to prepend to every metric

configOption.name: add_newline
configOption.synopsis: Append a newline to every event. This is useful if you want to fake out a server using netcat (nc -lu 8125)

configOption.name: meter_support
configOption.synopsis: Enable/disable the non-standard StatsD Meter type, if disabled falls back to counter and will append a "_meter" suffix to the metric name

parameter.name: freq
parameter.para: Frequency of the tone to wait for.

parameter.name: duration_ms
parameter.para: Minimum duration of tone, in ms. Default is 500ms. Using a minimum duration under 50ms is unlikely to produce accurate results.

parameter.name: timeout
parameter.para: Maximum amount of time, in seconds, to wait for specified tone. Default is forever.

parameter.name: times
parameter.para: Number of times the tone should be detected (subject to the provided timeout) before returning. Default is 1.

option.name: d
option.para: Custom decibel threshold to use. Default is 16.

option.name: s
option.para: Squelch tone.

description.para: Waits for a single-frequency tone to be detected before dialplan execution continues.

variable.name: WAITFORTONESTATUS
variable.para: This indicates the result of the wait.

application.name: ToneScan
application.synopsis: Wait for period of time while scanning for call progress tones

parameter.name: zone
parameter.para: Call progress zone. Default is the system default.

parameter.name: timeout
parameter.para: Maximum amount of time, in seconds, to wait for call progress or signal tones. Default is forever.

parameter.name: threshold
parameter.para: DSP threshold required for a match. A higher number will require a longer match and may reduce false positives, at the expense of false negatives. Default is 1.

option.name: f
option.para: Enable fax machine detection. By default, this is disabled.

option.name: v
option.para: Enable voice detection. By default, this is disabled.

description.para: Waits for a a distinguishable call progress tone and then exits. Unlike a conventional scanner, this is not currently capable of scanning for modem carriers.

variablelist.variable:
This indicates the result of the scan.
Audible ringback tone
Busy tone
Special Information Tones
Human voice detected
DTMF digit
Fax (answering)
Modem (answering)
Dial tone
UK Number Unobtainable tone
Timeout reached before any positive detection
Caller hung up before any positive detection

function.name: TONE_DETECT
function.synopsis: Asynchronously detects a tone

parameter.name: freq
parameter.para: Frequency of the tone to detect. To disable frequency detection completely (e.g. for signal detection only), specify 0 for the frequency.

parameter.name: duration_ms
parameter.para: Minimum duration of tone, in ms. Default is 500ms. Using a minimum duration under 50ms is unlikely to produce accurate results.

option.name: a
option.para: Match immediately on Special Information Tones, instead of or in addition to a particular frequency.

option.name: b
option.para: Match immediately on a busy signal, instead of or in addition to a particular frequency.

option.name: c
option.para: Match immediately on a dial tone, instead of or in addition to a particular frequency.

option.name: d
option.para: Custom decibel threshold to use. Default is 16.

option.name: e
option.para: Automatically end detection after desired number of hits (as specified in the n option.

option.name: g
option.para: Go to the specified context,exten,priority if tone is received on this channel. Detection will not end automatically, unless the e option is also specified.

option.name: h
option.para: Go to the specified context,exten,priority if tone is transmitted on this channel. Detection will not end automatically, unless the e option is also specified.

option.name: n
option.para: Number of times the tone should be detected (subject to the provided timeout) before going to the destination provided in the g or h option. Default is 1.

option.name: p
option.para: Match immediately on audible ringback tone, instead of or in addition to a particular frequency.

option.name: r
option.para: Apply to received frames only. Default is both directions.

option.name: s
option.para: Squelch tone.

option.name: t
option.para: Apply to transmitted frames only. Default is both directions.

option.name: x
option.para: Destroy the detector (stop detection).

description.para: The TONE_DETECT function detects a single-frequency tone and keeps track of how many times the tone has been detected.

When reading this function (instead of writing), supply tx to get the number of times a tone has been detected in the TX direction and rx to get the number of times a tone has been detected in the RX direction.
description.example: same => n,Set(TONE_DETECT(2600,1000,g(got-2600,s,1))=) ; detect 2600 Hz same => n,Wait(15) same => n,NoOp(${TONE_DETECT(rx)})
same => n,Set(TONE_DETECT(0,,bg(my-hangup,s,1))=) ; disconnect a call if we hear a busy signal same => n,Goto(somewhere-else) same => n(myhangup),Hangup()
same => n,Set(TONE_DETECT(0,,x)=) ; remove the detector from the channel

description.para: These config objects are currently shared by the following Asterisk capabilities:

enum.name: chan_websocket
enum.para: The WebSocket channel driver.

enum.name: res_ari
enum.para: ARI Outbound WebSockets.

description.para: They may have more specific information or restrictions on the parameters below.
description.example: ; ; A connection for use by chan_websocket [media_connection1] type = websocket_client uri = ws://localhost:8787 protocols = media username = media_username password = media_password connection_type = per_call_config connection_timeout = 500 reconnect_interval = 500 reconnect_attempts = 5 tls_enabled = no ; ; A TLS connection for use by ARI Outbound Websocket [ari_connection1] type = websocket_client uri = wss://localhost:8765 protocols = ari username = some_username password = some_password connection_type = persistent connection_timeout = 500 reconnect_interval = 500 reconnect_attempts = 5 tls_enabled = yes ca_list_file = /etc/pki/tls/cert.pem verify_server_cert = no verify_server_hostname = no

enum.name: per_call_config

configOption.name: connection_timeout

configOption.name: reconnect_attempts
configOption.synopsis: On failure, how many times should reconnection be attempted?

description.para: For per_call connections, this is the number of (re)connection attempts to make before returning an and terminating the call. Persistent connections always retry forever but this setting will control how often failure messages are logged.

configOption.name: reconnect_interval
configOption.synopsis: How often should reconnection be attempted (ms)?

configOption.name: tls_enabled
configOption.synopsis: Enable TLS

configOption.name: ca_list_file
configOption.synopsis: File containing the server's CA certificate. (optional)

configOption.name: ca_list_path
configOption.synopsis: Path to a directory containing one or more hashed CA certificates. (optional)

configOption.name: cert_file

configOption.name: priv_key_file
configOption.synopsis: File containing the client's private key. (optional)

configOption.name: verify_server_cert

application.name: JabberSend
application.synopsis: Sends an XMPP message to a buddy.

parameter.name: account
parameter.para: The local named account to listen on (specified in xmpp.conf)

parameter.name: jid
parameter.para: Jabber ID of the buddy to send the message to. It can be a bare JID (username@domain) or a full JID (username@domain/resource).

parameter.name: message
parameter.para: The message to send.

description.para: Sends the content of message as text message from the given account to the buddy identified by jid
The example below sends "Hello world" to bob@domain.com as an XMPP message from the account asterisk, configured in xmpp.conf.

function.name: JABBER_RECEIVE
function.synopsis: Reads XMPP messages.

parameter.name: account
parameter.para: The local named account to listen on (specified in xmpp.conf)

parameter.name: jid
parameter.para: Jabber ID of the buddy to receive message from. It can be a bare JID (username@domain) or a full JID (username@domain/resource).

parameter.name: timeout
parameter.para: In seconds, defaults to 20.

description.para: Receives a text message on the given account from the buddy identified by jid and returns the contents.
The example below returns an XMPP message sent from bob@domain.com (or nothing in case of a time out), to the asterisk XMPP account configured in xmpp.conf.

function.name: JABBER_STATUS

parameter.name: account

parameter.para: Jabber ID of the buddy to receive message from. It can be a bare JID (username@domain) or a full JID (username@domain/resource).

enum.para: Online

Away
Extended Away
Do Not Disturb
Offline
Not In Roster

description.para: Parameters for defining a Location object

enum.name: GML
enum.para: The location_info parameter must contain a comma separated list valid GML elements describing this location.

enum.name: URI

configOption.synopsis: Location information

configOption.name: location_source

configOption.name: method

configOption.name: confidence

Sub-parameters:

enum.name: pdf
enum.para: One of:

enum.name: value

configOption.synopsis: The content of the deviceID element

configOption.synopsis: Reference to a location object

configOption.synopsis: location specification type

description.para: xxxx

configOption.name: suppress_empty_ca_elements

configOption.name: profile_precedence
configOption.synopsis: Determine which profile on a channel should be used

enum.name: prefer_incoming
enum.para: Use the incoming profile if it exists and has location information, otherwise use the configured profile if it exists and has location information. If neither profile has location information, nothing is sent.

enum.name: prefer_config
enum.para: Use the configured profile if it exists and has location information, otherwise use the incoming profile if it exists and has location information. If neither profile has location information, nothing is sent.

enum.name: discard_incoming
enum.para: Discard any incoming profile and use the configured profile if it exists and it has location information. If the configured profile doesn't exist or has no location information, nothing is sent.

enum.name: discard_config
enum.para: Discard any configured profile and use the incoming profile if it exists and it has location information. If the incoming profile doesn't exist or has no location information, nothing is sent.

function.name: GEOLOC_PROFILE
function.synopsis: Get or Set a field in a geolocation profile

parameter.name: parameter
parameter.para: The profile parameter to operate on. The following fields from the Location and Profile objects are supported.
Additionally, the inheritable field may be set to true or false to control whether the profile will be passed to the outgoing channel.

option.name: a
option.para: Append provided value to the specified parameter instead of replacing the existing value. This only applies to variable list parameters like location_info_refinement.

option.name: r
option.para: Before reading or after writing the specified parameter, re-resolve the effective_location and usage_rules parameters using the location_variables parameter and the variables set on the channel in effect at the time this function is called.

note.para: On a read operation, this does not alter the actual profile in any way. On a write operation however, the effective_location and/or usage_rules parameters may indeed change and those changes will be passed on to any outgoing channel.

description.para: When used to set a parameter on a profile, if the profile doesn't already exist, a new one will be created automatically.
The ${GEOLOCPROFILESTATUS} channel variable will be set with a return code indicating the result of the operation. Possible values are:

enum.para: Success
No or not enough parameters were supplied
There was an internal error finding or creating a profile
There was an issue specific to the parameter specified (value not valid or parameter name not found, etc.)

description.para: The Endpoint is the primary configuration object. It contains the core SIP related options only, endpoints are NOT dialable entries of their own. Communication with another SIP device is accomplished via Addresses of Record (AoRs) which have one or more contacts associated with them. Endpoints NOT configured to use a transport will default to first transport found in pjsip.conf that matches its type.

Example: An Endpoint has been configured with no transport. When it comes time to call an AoR, PJSIP will find the first transport that matches the type. A SIP URI of sip:5000@[11::33] will use the first IPv6 transport and try to send the request.

If the anonymous endpoint identifier is in use an endpoint with the name "anonymous@domain" will be searched for as a last resort. If this is not found it will fall back to searching for "anonymous". If neither endpoints are found the anonymous endpoint identifier will not return an endpoint and anonymous calling will not be possible.

configOption.name: 100rel
configOption.synopsis: Allow support for RFC3262 provisional ACK tags

enum.name: no
enum.para: If set to no, do not support transmission of reliable provisional responses. As UAS, if an incoming request contains 100rel in the Required header, it is rejected with 420 Bad Extension.

enum.name: required
enum.para: If set to required, require provisional responses to be sent and received reliably. As UAS, incoming requests without 100rel in the Supported header are rejected with 421 Extension Required. As UAC, outgoing requests will have 100rel in the Required header.

enum.name: peer_supported
enum.para: If set to peer_supported, send provisional responses reliably if the request by the peer contained 100rel in the Supported or Require header. As UAS, if an incoming request contains 100rel in the Supported header, send 1xx responses reliably. If the request by the peer does not contain 100rel in the Supported and Require header, send responses normally. As UAC, outgoing requests will contain 100rel in the Supported header.

enum.name: yes
enum.para: If set to yes, indicate the support of reliable provisional responses and PRACK them if required by the peer. As UAS, if the incoming request contains 100rel in the Supported header but not in the Required header, send 1xx responses normally. If the incoming request contains 100rel in the Required header, send 1xx responses reliably. As UAC add 100rel to the Supported header and PRACK 1xx responses if required.

configOption.name: aggregate_mwi
configOption.synopsis: Condense MWI notifications into a single NOTIFY.

description.para: When enabled, aggregate_mwi condenses message waiting notifications from multiple mailboxes into a single NOTIFY. If it is disabled, individual NOTIFYs are sent for each mailbox.

configOption.name: allow
configOption.synopsis: Media Codec(s) to allow

configOption.name: codec_prefs_incoming_offer
configOption.synopsis: Codec negotiation prefs for incoming offers.

description.para: This is a string that describes how the codecs specified on an incoming SDP offer (pending) are reconciled with the codecs specified on an endpoint (configured) before being sent to the Asterisk core. The string actually specifies 4 name:value pair parameters separated by commas. Whitespace is ignored and they may be specified in any order. Note that this option is reserved for future functionality.
Parameters:

enum.name: pending
enum.para: The codec list from the caller. (default)

enum.name: configured
enum.para: The codec list from the endpoint.

enum.name: intersect
enum.para: Only common codecs with the preferred codecs first. (default)

enum.name: only_preferred
enum.para: Use only the preferred codecs.

enum.name: only_nonpreferred
enum.para: Use only the non-preferred codecs.

enum.name: all
enum.para: After the operation, keep all codecs. (default)

enum.name: first
enum.para: After the operation, keep only the first codec.

enum.name: allow
enum.para: Allow transcoding. (default)

enum.name: prevent
enum.para: Prevent transcoding.

description.example: codec_prefs_incoming_offer = prefer: pending, operation: intersect, keep: all, transcode: allow
description.para: Prefer the codecs coming from the caller. Use only the ones that are common. keeping the order of the preferred list. Keep all codecs in the result. Allow transcoding.

configOption.name: codec_prefs_outgoing_offer
configOption.synopsis: Codec negotiation prefs for outgoing offers.

description.para: This is a string that describes how the codecs specified in the topology that comes from the Asterisk core (pending) are reconciled with the codecs specified on an endpoint (configured) when sending an SDP offer. The string actually specifies 4 name:value pair parameters separated by commas. Whitespace is ignored and they may be specified in any order. Note that this option is reserved for future functionality.
Parameters:

enum.name: pending
enum.para: The codec list from the core. (default)

enum.name: configured
enum.para: The codec list from the endpoint.

enum.name: union
enum.para: Merge the lists with the preferred codecs first. (default)

enum.name: intersect
enum.para: Only common codecs with the preferred codecs first. (default)

enum.name: only_preferred
enum.para: Use only the preferred codecs.

enum.name: only_nonpreferred
enum.para: Use only the non-preferred codecs.

enum.name: all
enum.para: After the operation, keep all codecs. (default)

enum.name: first
enum.para: After the operation, keep only the first codec.

enum.name: allow
enum.para: Allow transcoding. (default)

enum.name: prevent
enum.para: Prevent transcoding.

description.example: codec_prefs_outgoing_offer = prefer: configured, operation: union, keep: first, transcode: prevent
description.para: Prefer the codecs coming from the endpoint. Merge them with the codecs from the core keeping the order of the preferred list. Keep only the first one. No transcoding allowed.

configOption.name: codec_prefs_incoming_answer
configOption.synopsis: Codec negotiation prefs for incoming answers.

description.para: This is a string that describes how the codecs specified in an incoming SDP answer (pending) are reconciled with the codecs specified on an endpoint (configured) when receiving an SDP answer. The string actually specifies 4 name:value pair parameters separated by commas. Whitespace is ignored and they may be specified in any order. Note that this option is reserved for future functionality.
Parameters:

enum.name: pending
enum.para: The codec list in the received SDP answer. (default)

enum.name: configured
enum.para: The codec list from the endpoint.

enum.name: union
enum.para: Merge the lists with the preferred codecs first.

enum.name: intersect
enum.para: Only common codecs with the preferred codecs first. (default)

enum.name: only_preferred
enum.para: Use only the preferred codecs.

enum.name: only_nonpreferred
enum.para: Use only the non-preferred codecs.

enum.name: all
enum.para: After the operation, keep all codecs. (default)

enum.name: first
enum.para: After the operation, keep only the first codec.

enum.name: transcode : < allow | prevent >
enum.para: The transcode parameter is ignored when processing answers.

description.para: Use the defaults but keep oinly the first codec.

configOption.name: codec_prefs_outgoing_answer
configOption.synopsis: Codec negotiation prefs for outgoing answers.

description.para: This is a string that describes how the codecs that come from the core (pending) are reconciled with the codecs specified on an endpoint (configured) when sending an SDP answer. The string actually specifies 4 name:value pair parameters separated by commas. Whitespace is ignored and they may be specified in any order. Note that this option is reserved for future functionality.
Parameters:

enum.name: pending
enum.para: The codec list that came from the core. (default)

enum.name: configured
enum.para: The codec list from the endpoint.

enum.name: union
enum.para: Merge the lists with the preferred codecs first.

enum.name: intersect
enum.para: Only common codecs with the preferred codecs first. (default)

enum.name: only_preferred
enum.para: Use only the preferred codecs.

enum.name: only_nonpreferred
enum.para: Use only the non-preferred codecs.

enum.name: all
enum.para: After the operation, keep all codecs. (default)

enum.name: first
enum.para: After the operation, keep only the first codec.

enum.name: transcode : < allow | prevent >
enum.para: The transcode parameter is ignored when processing answers.

description.para: Use the defaults but keep oinly the first codec.

configOption.name: allow_overlap

configOption.name: overlap_context

If specified, the extensions/patterns in the specified context will be used for determining if a full number has been received from the endpoint.

configOption.name: aors

Endpoints without an authentication object configured will allow connections without verification.

note.para: Using the same auth section for inbound and outbound authentication is not recommended. There is a difference in meaning for an empty realm setting between inbound and outbound authentication uses. See the auth realm description for details.

configOption.name: callerid
configOption.synopsis: CallerID information for the endpoint

configOption.name: callerid_privacy

configOption.name: direct_media_glare_mitigation
configOption.synopsis: Mitigation of direct media (re)INVITE glare

description.para: This setting attempts to avoid creating INVITE glare scenarios by disabling direct media reINVITEs in one direction thereby allowing designated servers (according to this option) to initiate direct media reINVITEs without contention and significantly reducing call setup time.

A more detailed description of how this option functions can be found in the Asterisk documentation https://docs.asterisk.org/Configuration/Channel-Drivers/SIP/Concepts/SIP-Direct-Media-Reinvite-Glare-Avoidance/

configOption.name: direct_media_method
configOption.synopsis: Direct Media method type

description.para: Method for setting up Direct Media between endpoints.

enum.name: reinvite
enum.para: Alias for the invite value.

configOption.name: trust_connected_line
configOption.synopsis: Accept Connected Line updates from this endpoint

configOption.name: send_connected_line
configOption.synopsis: Send Connected Line updates to this endpoint

configOption.name: connected_line_method
configOption.synopsis: Connected line method type

description.para: Method used when updating connected line information.

enum.name: invite
enum.para: When set to invite, check the remote's Allow header and if UPDATE is allowed, send UPDATE instead of INVITE to avoid SDP renegotiation. If UPDATE is not Allowed, send INVITE.

enum.name: reinvite
enum.para: Alias for the invite value.

enum.name: update
enum.para: If set to update, send UPDATE regardless of what the remote Allows.

configOption.name: direct_media
configOption.synopsis: Determines whether media may flow directly between endpoints.

configOption.name: disable_direct_media_on_nat
configOption.synopsis: Disable direct media session refreshes when NAT obstructs the media session

configOption.name: disallow
configOption.synopsis: Media Codec(s) to disallow

configOption.name: dtmf_mode
configOption.synopsis: DTMF mode

description.para: This setting allows to choose the DTMF mode for endpoint communication.

enum.name: rfc4733
enum.para: DTMF is sent out of band of the main audio stream.

enum.name: inband
enum.para: DTMF is sent as part of audio stream.

enum.name: info
enum.para: DTMF is sent as SIP INFO packets.

enum.name: auto
enum.para: DTMF is sent as RFC 4733 if the other side supports it or as INBAND if not.

enum.name: auto_info
enum.para: DTMF is sent as RFC 4733 if the other side supports it or as SIP INFO if not.

configOption.name: media_address
configOption.synopsis: IP address used in SDP for media handling

description.para: At the time of SDP creation, the IP address defined here will be used as the media address for individual streams in the SDP.
